```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat
import itertools
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from amab_process import adequacy as ad

DOC = "PCR-005"
UO = "protein_a"
UO_TITLE = "Protein A Chromatography (Step 5)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- formatting
def mn(s):
    """A number as the prose and this report's own tables print it, with a true minus sign."""
    return str(s).replace("-", "−")
def g(x):
    return f"{x:g}"
def lc(name):
    """A parameter name inside a sentence: the first letter lower-cased unless the name opens on an acronym."""
    return name if name[:2].isupper() else name[0].lower() + name[1:]
def rng(p):
    return f"{p.prange[0]:g}–{p.prange[1]:g}"
def nor(p):
    return f"{p.nor[0]:g}–{p.nor[1]:g}"
def f0(x):
    return f"{x:,.0f}"
def f1(x):
    return f"{x:,.1f}"
def f2(x):
    return f"{x:,.2f}"
def f3(x):
    return f"{x:.3f}"
def p3(p):
    return "< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}"
def pf(p):
    return "p < 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {p:.3f}"
def md_rows(md):
    """The rows of a markdown table a helper returns, as a frame, so that the report can set it as a numbered table."""
    lines = [l for l in md.strip().splitlines() if l.startswith("|")]
    cells = lambda l: [c.strip() for c in l.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
    return pd.DataFrame([cells(l) for l in lines[2:]], columns=cells(lines[0]))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- identity, dates
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
P = {p.key: p for p in uo.parameters}
ver, eff_date = doc_version(DOC)
scale_l = f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"
plan_appr = PLAN_APPROVAL["PCP-005"]
chron = csv("study_chronology.csv")
chron = chron[chron["step"] == UO].set_index("id")
def win(sid):
    return f"{chron.loc[sid, 'start']} to {chron.loc[sid, 'end']}"
PDS = {d["id"]: d for d in PLAN_DISCREPANCIES[DOC]}
n_pd = len(PDS)
pd_first, pd_last = list(PDS)[0], list(PDS)[-1]
assert list(PDS) == ["PD-005-01", "PD-005-02", "PD-005-03", "PD-005-04", "PD-005-05", "PD-005-06", "PD-005-07", "PD-005-08", "PD-005-09", "PD-005-10"]
assert "titre" in PDS["PD-005-06"]["done"] and "280 nm" in PDS["PD-005-06"]["planned"]
supp_studies = list(PDS["PD-005-01"]["studies"])
# the hold study S-PA-HLD was made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis, after INV-001 closed (PD-005-05)
assert PDS["PD-005-05"]["studies"] == ["S-PA-HLD"]
rean_studies = [s_ for d_ in PDS.values() for s_ in d_.get("studies", [])]
assert rean_studies == supp_studies + ["S-PA-HLD"]
chron_char = chron.drop(index=rean_studies)
first_start = chron_char["start"].min()
last_end = chron_char["end"].max()
assert all(chron.loc[s, "start"] > last_end for s in rean_studies)    # the re-analysis studies came after
assert chron.loc["S-PA-HLD", "start"] > INV["closed"] and chron.loc["S-PA-HLD", "start"] > AMD["date"]
assert (chron["start"] > plan_appr).all()                              # every study after plan approval
# NORs come from production (owner, 2026-10-11): an offset never narrows a NOR, so no NOR and no
# set-point of the step changes in this revision
NOR_CHANGED = [p.key for p in uo.parameters if list(p.nor) != list(p.nor_characterized)]
assert NOR_CHANGED == []
assert all(float(p.setpoint) == float(p.setpoint_characterized) for p in uo.parameters)
# no NOR of the step lies outside its corrected PAR (D.nor_flags): the flag of this report comes from the
# qualification of the scale-down model for pool HCP, not from a PAR
nor_flag_rows = D.nor_flags(UO)
assert nor_flag_rows.empty
ca3_date = CAMPAIGN["model_adequacy"]["selection_adopted"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- design structure
n_scr = doe_runs(UO, "screening"); n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
cp_scr = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening"); cp_rsm = doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
n_fact = n_scr - cp_scr
n_axial = n_rsm - n_fact - cp_rsm
FAC = D.rsm_factors(UO)
n_fac = len(FAC)
LT = D.factor_letters(UO)                                       # load -> A, ...
# the design centre is the set-point of every design factor, so set-point and design-centre
# analyses coincide at this step
assert all(abs(D.to_coded(UO, q, P[q].setpoint)) < 1e-9 for q in FAC)
rp = report_params(UO)
n_par = len(rp)
n_multi = int((rp["Study"] == "multivariate").sum()); n_uni = n_par - n_multi
CLS = dict(zip(rp["Parameter"], rp["Class"]))
assert CLS == {"Protein load": "WC-CPP", "Elution buffer pH": "WC-CPP", "Load flow rate": "KPP",
               "End of pool collect": "KPP", "Operating temperature": "GPP", "Bed height": "GPP"}
cls = rp["Class"].value_counts()
n_wc = int(cls.get("WC-CPP", 0)); n_cpp = int(cls.get("CPP", 0)); n_kpp = int(cls.get("KPP", 0)); n_gpp = int(cls.get("GPP", 0))
rt_set = P["bed_height"].setpoint / P["flow"].setpoint * 60
rt_hi = P["bed_height"].setpoint / P["flow"].prange[1] * 60
rt_lo = P["bed_height"].setpoint / P["flow"].prange[0] * 60
rt_short = P["bed_height"].prange[0] / P["flow"].setpoint * 60
wr = [(p.prange[1] - p.prange[0]) / (p.nor[1] - p.nor[0]) for p in uo.parameters]
wr_min, wr_max = min(wr), max(wr)
mc_n = f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- criteria of the Protein A pool
RESP_C = ["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "leached_protein_a_ppm", "lmw_cesds_pct"]
iac = D.iac_table(UO).set_index("response")
acc = {r: D.effective_acceptance(UO, r) for r in RESP_C}
n_crit = len(acc)
C_HCP, C_LPA, C_FRAG = (acc[r][1] for r in RESP_C)
crit_hcp = f0(C_HCP); crit_lpa = f0(C_LPA); crit_frag = f2(C_FRAG)
ds_hcp = g(iac.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "ds_high"]); ds_lpa = g(iac.loc["leached_protein_a_ppm", "ds_high"])
ds_frag = f2(iac.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "ds_high"])
fold_hcp = f0(iac.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "downstream_fold"]); fold_lpa = g(iac.loc["leached_protein_a_ppm", "downstream_fold"])
fold_frag = f2(iac.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "downstream_fold"]); add_frag = f2(iac.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "downstream_added"])
apri_hcp = f0(iac.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "iac_high_apriori"])
widened = {r: bool(iac.loc[r, "widened"]) for r in RESP_C}
tightened = {r: bool(iac.loc[r, "tightened"]) for r in RESP_C}
assert widened["pool_hcp_ng_mg"] and not widened["leached_protein_a_ppm"] and not widened["lmw_cesds_pct"]
assert not any(tightened.values())
assert iac.loc["leached_protein_a_ppm", "iac_high"] == iac.loc["leached_protein_a_ppm", "iac_high_apriori"]
assert iac.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "iac_high"] == iac.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "iac_high_apriori"]
r1 = D.rev1_criteria(UO).set_index("response")
r1_hcp = f0(r1.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "high"]); r1_margin = g(r1.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "margin"])
assert C_HCP > r1.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "high"]                       # wider than Version 1.0
eff_alpha = THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"]; lof_alpha = THRESHOLDS["lof_alpha"]; max_gap = THRESHOLDS["max_r2_minus_pred_r2"]
TH = {k: float(v) for k, v in THRESHOLDS.items()}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- criteria of the held eluate (production bioreactor output)
bio = D.iac_table("bioreactor").set_index("response")
agg_lim = D.iac_limit("bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw"); acid_lim = D.iac_limit("bioreactor", "acidic_variants")
assert agg_lim[2] == "upper" and acid_lim[2] == "two_sided"
agg_crit = f2(agg_lim[1]); acid_crit = f"{acid_lim[0]:g}–{acid_lim[1]:g}"
agg_ds = g(bio.loc["aggregates_hmw", "ds_high"]); agg_apri = f2(bio.loc["aggregates_hmw", "iac_high_apriori"])
acid_ds_hi = g(bio.loc["acidic_variants", "ds_high"]); acid_apri_hi = f1(bio.loc["acidic_variants", "iac_high_apriori"])
assert bool(bio.loc["aggregates_hmw", "tightened"]) and bool(bio.loc["aggregates_hmw", "widened"])
assert agg_lim[1] < bio.loc["aggregates_hmw", "iac_high_apriori"]       # the net change is stricter
assert not bool(bio.loc["acidic_variants", "widened"]) and not bool(bio.loc["acidic_variants", "tightened"])
assert acid_lim[1] == bio.loc["acidic_variants", "iac_high_apriori"]       # the a priori value
assert acid_lim[0] == bio.loc["acidic_variants", "ds_low"]              # the lower limit is the drug substance one

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the downstream values these criteria rely on
ver_all = D.iac_verification()
VR = {(r["step_key"], r["cqa"]): r for _, r in ver_all[ver_all["step_key"].isin(["viral_inactivation", "cex", "aex", "ufdf"])].iterrows()}
n_ver_rows = len(VR)
v_cex_hcp, v_aex_hcp = VR[("cex", "hcp")], VR[("aex", "hcp")]
v_cex_frag, v_vi_frag = VR[("cex", "fragments_lmw")], VR[("viral_inactivation", "fragments_lmw")]
v_cex_lpa, v_aex_lpa = VR[("cex", "leached_protein_a")], VR[("aex", "leached_protein_a")]
v_cex_agg, v_vi_agg, v_vi_acid = VR[("cex", "aggregates_hmw")], VR[("viral_inactivation", "aggregates_hmw")], VR[("viral_inactivation", "acidic_variants")]
n_ver_pool = 6; n_ver_hold = 4
assert n_ver_rows == n_ver_pool + n_ver_hold
# host cell protein, on the single-batch rule (owner, 2026-10-09; PCMP-001 §7.5): cation exchange meets its
# platform value at the point prediction, so no tightening, but not at the single-batch bound, so no widening
# and the platform value stands; anion exchange beats its platform value at the single-batch bound, on an
# adequate model, and widens the criterion
assert D.VERIFICATION_BOUND == 0.95
for v in (v_cex_hcp, v_aex_hcp):
    assert bool(v["met"]) and bool(v["model_adequate"]) and v["assumed"] > v["observed_edge"]
    assert v["r2_minus_pred_r2"] <= max_gap and v["p_lack_of_fit"] >= lof_alpha
assert v_cex_hcp["predicted_nor"] >= v_cex_hcp["assumed"] > v_cex_hcp["predicted_nor_bound95"]
assert not bool(v_cex_hcp["widening_supported"])
assert v_aex_hcp["predicted_nor_bound95"] > v_aex_hcp["assumed"] and bool(v_aex_hcp["widening_supported"])
# fragments: both point predictions meet the platform values, neither single-batch bound beats them, and
# neither model is adequate, so the platform values stand
assert v_cex_frag["predicted_nor_bound95"] < v_cex_frag["assumed"] and v_vi_frag["predicted_nor_bound95"] > v_vi_frag["assumed"]
for v in (v_cex_frag, v_vi_frag):
    assert bool(v["met"]) and not bool(v["model_adequate"]) and not bool(v["widening_supported"])
    assert v["r2_minus_pred_r2"] > max_gap
# leached Protein A: not a response downstream
assert pd.isna(v_cex_lpa["met"]) and pd.isna(v_aex_lpa["met"])
# hold criteria: cation exchange aggregate tightened, low-pH inactivation aggregate and acidic variants widened
assert not bool(v_cex_agg["met"]) and bool(v_vi_agg["widening_supported"]) and not bool(v_vi_acid["widening_supported"])
# the low-pH acidic-variant bound is better than the platform value, but its model fits exactly and is not adequate
assert v_vi_acid["predicted_nor_bound95"] < v_vi_acid["assumed"] and not bool(v_vi_acid["model_adequate"])
_vi_acid_fit = D.fit("viral_inactivation", "rsm", "acidic_variants")
assert _vi_acid_fit["status"] == "none" and bool(_vi_acid_fit["exact"])
fold_check = v_cex_hcp["assumed"] * v_aex_hcp["predicted_nor_bound95"]
assert abs(fold_check - iac.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "downstream_fold"]) / fold_check < 1e-3
assert abs(bio.loc["aggregates_hmw", "downstream_fold"] - v_cex_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"]) < 1e-3
# the aggregate added after the low-pH step: its single-batch bound plus the UF/DF allowance (owner, 2026-10-11)
v_ufdf_agg = VR[("ufdf", "aggregates_hmw")]
assert float(v_ufdf_agg["assumed"]) == 0 and not bool(v_ufdf_agg["met"])      # PCMP-001 assumed no change; UF/DF tightens
assert abs(bio.loc["aggregates_hmw", "downstream_added"] - v_vi_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"] - v_ufdf_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"]) < 1e-3
assert abs(bio.loc["acidic_variants", "downstream_added"] - v_vi_acid["assumed"]) < 1e-9          # the platform value stands
n_rsm_cex = doe_runs("cex", "rsm"); n_rsm_aex = doe_runs("aex", "rsm")
assert UO not in CFG.raw()["iac"]["platform"]          # no upstream criterion relies on a Protein A worst case
cp_rsm_cex = doe_centre_points("cex", "rsm"); cp_rsm_aex = doe_centre_points("aex", "rsm")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the selected response-surface models (PD-005-04)
RESP = ["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "step_yield", "leached_protein_a_ppm", "lmw_cesds_pct"]
F = {r: D.fit(UO, "rsm", r) for r in RESP}
fH, fY, fL, fF = (F[r] for r in RESP)
assert all(F[r]["status"] == "selected" and F[r]["adequate"] for r in RESP)
assert fH["transform"] == "log" and all(F[r]["transform"] is None for r in RESP[1:])
assert not any(F[r]["block"] for r in RESP) and not D.has_augmentation(UO)
bc = fH["boxcox"]
assert bc["lo"] <= 0 <= bc["hi"] and not (bc["lo"] <= 1 <= bc["hi"])
assert all(F[r]["boxcox"] is None or F[r]["boxcox"]["lo"] <= 1 <= F[r]["boxcox"]["hi"] for r in RESP[1:])
def term_code(t):
    if ":" in t:
        a, b = t.split(":")
        return LT[a] + LT[b]
    if t.endswith("^2"):
        return LT[t[:-2]] + "²"
    return LT[t]
TERMS = {r: [term_code(t) for t in F[r]["names"]] for r in RESP}
assert TERMS["pool_hcp_ng_mg"] == ["A", "B", "C", "D", "C²"]
assert TERMS["step_yield"] == ["A", "C", "D", "AC", "D²"]
assert TERMS["leached_protein_a_ppm"] == []
assert TERMS["lmw_cesds_pct"] == ["A", "B"]
n_terms_full = len(ad.full_terms(FAC))
n_terms = {r: len(TERMS[r]) for r in RESP}
for r in RESP:
    f = F[r]
    assert f["gap"] <= max_gap and f["p_lof"] >= lof_alpha and (not f["names"] or f["p"] < eff_alpha)
# the planned full quadratic models
full_pred_neg = [r for r in ["leached_protein_a_ppm", "lmw_cesds_pct"] if F[r]["full"]["predR2"] < 0]
assert full_pred_neg == ["leached_protein_a_ppm", "lmw_cesds_pct"]
assert all(F[r]["full"]["gap"] > 2 * max_gap for r in full_pred_neg)
p_lof_raw_full = fH["full"]["p_lof"]                    # pool HCP, full quadratic, raw scale, run 23 at its recorded pH
assert p_lof_raw_full < lof_alpha
assert fY["full"]["gap"] > max_gap
# the interaction of protein load with elution buffer pH: tested where the selection dropped it
p_ab_log = float(fH["full_scale"]["model"].pvalues["load:elution_ph"])
p_ab_raw = float(fH["full"]["model"].pvalues["load:elution_ph"])
assert p_ab_log >= eff_alpha and p_ab_raw < eff_alpha and "load:elution_ph" not in fH["names"]
with D.planned_full_models():
    p_ab_v1 = float(D.fit(UO, "rsm", "pool_hcp_ng_mg")["model"].pvalues["load:elution_ph"])
assert p_ab_v1 < eff_alpha                               # the Version 1.0 model carried it
# INV-002: the remedy its rule gave each full quadratic model of this step (no augmentation)
ma = csv("model_adequacy.csv"); ma = ma[ma["step_key"] == UO].set_index("response")
assert ma.loc["leached_protein_a_ppm", "reason"] == "no effect to resolve"
assert ma.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "reason"] == "assurance not reached within the size of the planned design"
assert (ma["remedy"] != "augment").all()

# coefficients of the selected models
cH = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg").set_index("Term")
kA, kB, kC, kD, kC2 = (float(cH.loc[t, "Coef."]) for t in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "C²"])
pA, pB, pC, pD, pC2 = (float(cH.loc[t, "p-value"]) for t in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "C²"])
assert kA > 0 > kB and kD < 0 and kC2 > 0 and pA < eff_alpha and pB < eff_alpha and pD < eff_alpha
assert pC >= eff_alpha and pC2 < eff_alpha
assert min(abs(kA), abs(kB)) > max(abs(kC), abs(kD), abs(kC2))       # the two largest coefficients
_hres = fH["model"].resid.values
(_osm, _osr), _ = sstat.probplot(_hres / fH["rmse"])
assert _osr[-1] < _osm[-1] and _osr[-2] < _osm[-2]                  # a short upper tail on the normal plot
fac_A = np.exp(2 * kA)                        # the factor across the range studied of protein load
fac_B = np.exp(-2 * kB)                       # the factor by which pool HCP falls from low to high pH
fall_D = 100 * (1 - np.exp(2 * kD))           # % fall across the range of end of pool collect
fall_D_nor = 100 * (1 - np.exp(2 * kD * D.to_coded(UO, "end_collect", P["end_collect"].nor[1])))
flow_hi = 100 * (np.exp(kC + kC2) - 1)        # % above set-point at the top of the flow range
flow_lo = 100 * (np.exp(-kC + kC2) - 1)       # and at the bottom
_cfn = [float(D.to_coded(UO, "flow", v)) for v in P["flow"].nor]
flow_nor = 100 * max(np.exp(kC * c + kC2 * c * c) - 1 for c in _cfn)
assert flow_hi > 0 and flow_lo > 0
# the same factor at both loads is a different amount in ng/mg
def hcp_m(nat):
    return float(D.to_mfg(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", D.predict(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", natural=nat))[0])
ph_lo, ph_hi = P["elution_ph"].prange
ld_lo, ld_hi = P["load"].prange
drop_hi_load = hcp_m({"load": ld_hi, "elution_ph": ph_lo}) - hcp_m({"load": ld_hi, "elution_ph": ph_hi})
drop_lo_load = hcp_m({"load": ld_lo, "elution_ph": ph_lo}) - hcp_m({"load": ld_lo, "elution_ph": ph_hi})
assert drop_hi_load > drop_lo_load > 0

cY = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "step_yield").set_index("Term")
yA, yC, yD, yAC, yD2 = (100 * float(cY.loc[t, "Coef."]) for t in ["A", "C", "D", "AC", "D²"])
y0 = 100 * float(cY.loc["Intercept", "Coef."])
yC_hi = yC + yAC; yC_lo = yC - yAC                       # flow coefficient at high and at low load
yD_lo_sp = yD - yD2; yD_sp_hi = yD + yD2                 # gain from low end to set-point, set-point to high end
assert yD > 0 and yA < 0 and yC_hi < 0 and abs(yC_lo) < abs(yC_hi) and yD2 < 0 and yD_sp_hi < yD_lo_sp
assert abs(yD) == max(abs(yA), abs(yC), abs(yD), abs(yAC), abs(yD2))
assert abs(yC_lo) < 0.1 * abs(yC_hi)                                 # almost no effect at low load

cF = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct").set_index("Term")
kFA, kFB = float(cF.loc["A", "Coef."]), float(cF.loc["B", "Coef."])
pFA, pFB = float(cF.loc["A", "p-value"]), float(cF.loc["B", "p-value"])
assert kFB < 0 and pFB < eff_alpha and pFA >= eff_alpha
_mainF = {q: abs(float(cF.loc[LT[q], "Coef."])) for q in FAC if LT[q] in cF.index}
gov_frag = max(_mainF, key=_mainF.get)
assert gov_frag == "elution_ph"
assert fF["R2"] < 0.5 and "C" not in TERMS["lmw_cesds_pct"] and "C" not in TERMS["leached_protein_a_ppm"]
gov_hcp = D.governing_factor(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
assert gov_hcp == "elution_ph" and abs(kB) > abs(kA)

lpa_mean = float(fL["model"].params["const"])
lpa_mean_m = float(D.to_mfg(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm", lpa_mean))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- criterion 5: residuals and influential runs
# the corpus definition (D.residual_influence, 2026-10-10): the regressions of the absolute residuals on the
# predicted values and of the residuals on run order at residual_alpha, Cook's distance against cook_factor/n.
# It agreed exactly with this report's own computation, which it replaces (asserted before removal, 2026-10-10).
res_alpha = THRESHOLDS["residual_alpha"]; cook_k = THRESHOLDS["cook_factor"]
cook_rule = f"{cook_k:g}/n"
RI = {r: D.residual_influence(UO, r) for r in RESP}
assert all(RI[r]["testable"] and RI[r]["n"] == n_rsm and RI[r]["runs"] == [int(x) for x in F[r]["df"]["run"]] for r in RESP)
cook_lim = RI["pool_hcp_ng_mg"]["cook_limit"]

# the upper prediction limit over the NOR, at manufacturing scale, for any selected model

def nor_upper(sel, resp, end="offset"):
    up = sel["model"].get_prediction(ad.matrix(GN, sel["terms"], False)).summary_frame(alpha=0.05)["obs_ci_upper"].to_numpy()
    up = np.exp(up) if sel["scale"] == "log" else up
    o = D.sdm_offset(UO, resp)
    if o is None:
        return float(up.max())
    v = o[end]
    return float(up.max() / v) if o["scale"] == "ratio" else float(up.max() - v)

    _G = pd.DataFrame({"coded_" + f: [float(D.to_coded(UO, f, g_[i])) for g_ in _grid] for i, f in enumerate(FAC)})
    _u = fH["model"].get_prediction(ad.matrix(_G, fH["names"], False)).summary_frame(alpha=0.05)["obs_ci_upper"].to_numpy()
    return float(np.exp(_u).max() / off_hcp["lo"])

# A grid point is inside when both ends of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run lie within the criterion of
# every quality attribute at manufacturing scale (D.design_space_grid, basis "batch"). One grid for every fraction.
DS_N = 41
ds = D.design_space_grid(UO, n=DS_N)

# the single-batch definition checked on the same grid, through the public prediction interval at manufacturing
# scale, for every output with a criterion
_gr = np.meshgrid(*[np.linspace(-1, 1, DS_N)] * n_fac, indexing="ij")
_cd = {f: g_.ravel() for f, g_ in zip(FAC, _gr)}
_nv = {f: (P[f].prange[0] + P[f].prange[1]) / 2 + _cd[f] * (P[f].prange[1] - P[f].prange[0]) / 2 for f in FAC}
def _batch_ok(resp, nat):
    """Both ends of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run within the criterion, at manufacturing scale."""
    _, lo_, hi_ = D.prediction_interval(UO, resp, nat)
    lo_m, hi_m = np.asarray(D.to_mfg(UO, resp, lo_)), np.asarray(D.to_mfg(UO, resp, hi_))
    return (lo_m >= acc[resp][0]) & (hi_m <= acc[resp][1])
_okb = {r: _batch_ok(r, _nv) for r in RESP_C}
assert _okb["leached_protein_a_ppm"].all() and _okb["lmw_cesds_pct"].all()      # neither excludes a point
_bad = ~_okb["pool_hcp_ng_mg"]
assert abs((1 - _bad.mean()) - ds["fraction"]) < 1e-12 and _bad.any()
_in = {f: (_nv[f] >= P[f].nor[0] - 1e-9) & (_nv[f] <= P[f].nor[1] + 1e-9) for f in FAC}
_inAB = _in["load"] & _in["elution_ph"]; _inCD = _in["flow"] & _in["end_collect"]
ds_load_min = float(_nv["load"][_bad].min()); ds_ph_max = float(_nv["elution_ph"][_bad].max())
# with all four factors inside their NORs no point is excluded
assert not np.any(_bad & _inAB & _inCD)
# with load flow rate and end of pool collect within their NORs the excluded region reaches into the protein load NOR
# (at low pH) and into the elution buffer pH NOR (at high load), but never into both
ds_nor_load_min = float(_nv["load"][_bad & _inCD].min()); ds_nor_ph_max = float(_nv["elution_ph"][_bad & _inCD].max())
assert ds_nor_load_min < P["load"].nor[1] and ds_nor_ph_max > P["elution_ph"].nor[0]
assert ds_load_min <= ds_nor_load_min and ds_ph_max >= ds_nor_ph_max
# inside both of those NORs a point is excluded only with load flow rate and end of pool collect below their NORs
_bad_ab = _bad & _inAB
assert _bad_ab.any()
# every such point has load flow rate outside its NOR: most below it, with end of pool collect low, and a few at
# the upper end of the flow range studied, at the highest load of the NOR and the lower end of the end-collect range
assert not np.any(_bad_ab & _in["flow"])
_ab_lo = _bad_ab & (_nv["flow"] < P["flow"].nor[0]); _ab_hi = _bad_ab & (_nv["flow"] > P["flow"].nor[1])
ds_ab_flow_max = float(_nv["flow"][_ab_lo].max()); ds_ab_ec_max = float(_nv["end_collect"][_ab_lo].max())
assert ds_ab_ec_max < P["end_collect"].setpoint
assert _ab_hi.any() and float(_nv["flow"][_ab_hi].min()) == P["flow"].prange[1]
assert float(_nv["end_collect"][_ab_hi].max()) == P["end_collect"].prange[0]
assert set(_nv["load"][_ab_hi]) == {float(P["load"].nor[1])}
# the plane of protein load and elution buffer pH at fixed settings of the other two
_g2 = np.linspace(-1, 1, DS_N); _A, _B = np.meshgrid(_g2, _g2)
def _nat2(c, d):
    return {"load": (ld_lo + ld_hi) / 2 + _A.ravel() * (ld_hi - ld_lo) / 2,
            "elution_ph": (ph_lo + ph_hi) / 2 + _B.ravel() * (ph_hi - ph_lo) / 2,
            "flow": np.full(_A.size, float(D.to_natural(UO, "flow", c))),
            "end_collect": np.full(_A.size, float(D.to_natural(UO, "end_collect", d)))}
def ds2(c, d):
    return 100 * float(np.mean(_batch_ok("pool_hcp_ng_mg", _nat2(c, d))))
ds2_sp = ds2(0, 0)
_cn = [float(D.to_coded(UO, "flow", v)) for v in P["flow"].nor]; _dn = [float(D.to_coded(UO, "end_collect", v)) for v in P["end_collect"].nor]
_nor2 = [ds2(c, d) for c in _cn for d in _dn]
ds2_nor_min, ds2_nor_max = min(_nor2), max(_nor2)
_rng2 = [ds2(c, d) for c in (-1, 1) for d in (-1, 1)]
ds2_rng_min, ds2_rng_max = min(_rng2), max(_rng2)
assert ds2_sp < 100 and ds2_rng_min <= ds2_nor_min
_spCD = (np.abs(_cd["flow"]) < 1e-9) & (np.abs(_cd["end_collect"]) < 1e-9)
_bad_sp = _bad & _spCD
assert _bad_sp.any() and not np.any(_bad_sp & _inAB)
assert abs(100 * (1 - _bad_sp.sum() / _spCD.sum()) - ds2_sp) < 1e-9          # the plane is a slice of the grid
# the edges of that corner with the other two at their set-points, on the continuous model
def hcp_up(nat):
    """The upper prediction limit of a single run at manufacturing scale; omitted factors sit at their set-points."""
    return float(D.to_mfg(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", D.prediction_interval(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", {k: [v] for k, v in nat.items()})[2])[0])
corner_sp = hcp_m({"load": ld_hi, "elution_ph": ph_lo})
corner_up = hcp_up({"load": ld_hi, "elution_ph": ph_lo})
nor_corner_up = hcp_up({"load": P["load"].nor[1], "elution_ph": P["elution_ph"].nor[0]})
assert corner_up > corner_sp > C_HCP >= nor_corner_up
ds_b_load = _brentq(lambda x: hcp_up({"load": x, "elution_ph": ph_lo}) - C_HCP, P["load"].setpoint, ld_hi)
ds_b_ph = _brentq(lambda x: hcp_up({"load": ld_hi, "elution_ph": x}) - C_HCP, ph_lo, ph_hi)
ds_b_ph_nor = _brentq(lambda x: hcp_up({"load": P["load"].nor[1], "elution_ph": x}) - C_HCP, ph_lo, P["elution_ph"].nor[0])
ds_b_load_nor = _brentq(lambda x: hcp_up({"load": x, "elution_ph": P["elution_ph"].nor[0]}) - C_HCP, P["load"].nor[1], ld_hi)
assert ds_b_load < P["load"].nor[1] and ds_b_ph > P["elution_ph"].nor[0]          # into each NOR on its own
assert ds_b_ph_nor < P["elution_ph"].nor[0] and ds_b_load_nor > P["load"].nor[1]  # not into both
assert (_nv["load"][_bad_sp] >= ds_b_load - 1e-9).all() and (_nv["elution_ph"][_bad_sp] <= ds_b_ph + 1e-9).all()
# medians over the NOR, as the criteria table computes them
_natg = {f: [g_[i] for g_ in NOR_GRID] for i, f in enumerate(FAC)}
_hn = np.asarray(D.to_mfg(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", D.predict(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", natural=_natg)))
hcp_nor_med_lo, hcp_nor_med_hi = float(_hn.min()), float(_hn.max())

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- hold study
hold = csv(f"hold_{UO}.csv")
temps = list(hold["temperature"].unique())
t_cold, t_warm = temps[0], temps[1]
h_days = int(hold["day"].max())
h_daylist = join_and([str(int(x)) for x in sorted(hold["day"].unique())])
ce_days = sorted(int(x) for x in hold.loc[hold["lmw_cesds_pct"].notna(), "day"].unique())
ce_days_txt = join_and([str(x) for x in ce_days])
ND = {"hmw_pct": 2, "acidic_pct": 1, "lmw_cesds_pct": 2}
def hr(t, d, c):
    """A hold result as the hold stability table shows it."""
    return round(float(hold[(hold["temperature"] == t) & (hold["day"] == d)][c].iloc[0]), ND[c])
def changes(t, c):
    days = sorted(int(x) for x in hold.loc[(hold["temperature"] == t) & hold[c].notna(), "day"])
    return [round(hr(t, d, c) - hr(t, 0, c), ND[c]) for d in days if d > 0]
d0 = {c: round(abs(hr(t_cold, 0, c) - hr(t_warm, 0, c)), ND[c]) for c in ND}
chg = {(t, c): round(hr(t, h_days, c) - hr(t, 0, c), ND[c]) for t in temps for c in ND}
inc = {(t, c): max(changes(t, c)) for t in temps for c in ND}
fall = {t: min(0.0, min(changes(t, "acidic_pct"))) for t in temps}
acid_fall = min(fall.values())
for t in temps:
    for c in ND:
        assert inc[(t, c)] == chg[(t, c)]                    # the largest increase is the one at the last day
assert chg[(t_warm, "hmw_pct")] > chg[(t_cold, "hmw_pct")] and chg[(t_warm, "acidic_pct")] == chg[(t_cold, "acidic_pct")]
assert chg[(t_cold, "lmw_cesds_pct")] > 0 and chg[(t_warm, "lmw_cesds_pct")] > 0
frag_gap = round(abs(chg[(t_warm, "lmw_cesds_pct")] - chg[(t_cold, "lmw_cesds_pct")]), ND["lmw_cesds_pct"])
assert chg[(t_warm, "lmw_cesds_pct")] > chg[(t_cold, "lmw_cesds_pct")] and frag_gap > d0["lmw_cesds_pct"]

assert all(chg[(t, c)] > 0 for t in temps for c in ND)          # every largest increase is positive: the hold rule adds it

HOLD_ROWS = []
for col, name, side, expv, crit_v in [("hmw_pct", "Aggregate, HMW", "Upper", exp_agg, agg_lim[1]),

                              Criterion=(f"≤ {crit_v:.{nd}f}" if side == "Upper" else f"≥ {crit_v:g}"),
                              Temperature=t, Change=mn(f"{ch_:+.{nd}f}") if ch_ else f"{0:.{nd}f}", Sum=f"{tot:.{nd}f}",
                              Met="Yes" if ok_ else "No", tot=tot, crit=crit_v, ok=ok_))

acid_lower_met = all(r["ok"] for r in HOLD_ROWS if r["Limit"] == "Lower")

uni_rows, UNI = [], {}
for prm in uni["parameter"].unique():
    for lvl in ["low", "high"]:
        g_ = uni[(uni["parameter"] == prm) & (uni["level"] == lvl)]
        row = [P[prm].name, f"{g_['value'].iloc[0]:g} {P[prm].unit}"]
        for r in UNI_RESP:
            k = 100 if r == "step_yield" else 1
            a = g_[r].values * k; b = uni_ref[r].values * k
            dfp = len(a) + len(b) - 2
            sp_ = np.sqrt(((len(a) - 1) * a.var(ddof=1) + (len(b) - 1) * b.var(ddof=1)) / dfp)
            hw = sstat.t.ppf(0.975, dfp) * sp_ * np.sqrt(1 / len(a) + 1 / len(b))
            dd_ = a.mean() - b.mean()
            nd = 0 if r == "pool_hcp_ng_mg" else (1 if r == "step_yield" else 2)
            UNI[(prm, lvl, r)] = dict(diff=dd_, lo=dd_ - hw, hi=dd_ + hw)
            row += [mn(f"{dd_:,.{nd}f}"), mn(f"{dd_ - hw:,.{nd}f} to {dd_ + hw:,.{nd}f}")]
        uni_rows.append(row)

def half_rms(m):
    """Root mean square of the residuals in the lower and in the upper half of the predicted values."""
    f_, r_ = m.fittedvalues.values, m.resid.values
    med_ = np.median(f_)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(r_[f_ <= med_] ** 2))), float(np.sqrt(np.mean(r_[f_ > med_] ** 2)))

def tname(t):
    """A model term in words, as the text names it."""

    if ":" in t:
        a, b = t.split(":")
        return f"the interaction of {nm(a)} with {nm(b)}"
    if t.endswith("^2"):
        return f"the square of {nm(t[:-2])}"
    return nm(t)

COOKSIM = {}
for r in RESP:

    _n, _p = _X.shape
    _H = _X @ np.linalg.pinv(_X.T @ _X) @ _X.T
    _h = np.diag(_H)
    _E = (np.eye(_n) - _H) @ _rngc.normal(size=(_n, D.PAR_MC_N))
    _Dk = (_E ** 2) / (_p * (_E ** 2).sum(0) / (_n - _p)) * (_h / (1 - _h) ** 2)[:, None]
    _cnt = (_Dk > cook_k / _n).sum(0)
    COOKSIM[r] = (float(_cnt.mean()), float((_cnt >= 1).mean()))

def app_info(kind):
    d = dS if kind == "screening" else dY
    out = pd.DataFrame({"Run": d["run"].astype(int).astype(str), "Run order": d["run_order"].astype(int).astype(str)})

    out["HMW by SEC (%)"] = d["hmw_sec_pct"].map(lambda x: f"{x:.2f}")
    out["DNA, load (pg/mg)"] = d["dna_load_pg_mg"].map(lambda x: x if pd.isna(x) else f"{x:,.0f}")
    out["DNA, pool (pg/mg)"] = d["dna_pool_pg_mg"].map(lambda x: x if pd.isna(x) else f"{x:,.0f}")
    return out

def _unit(u):
    return _re.sub(r"\s*\([^)]*\)", "", str(u)).strip()
def _crit(r):
    u = _unit(r["unit"])
    if r["spec_type"] == "upper":
        return f"≤ {r['acc_high']:g} {u}"
    if r["spec_type"] == "lower":
        return f"≥ {r['acc_low']:g} {u}"
    return f"{r['acc_low']:g}–{r['acc_high']:g} {u}"
def _side(k):
    r = capf.loc[k]
    if r["spec_type"] != "two_sided":
        return r["spec_type"]
    return "lower" if r["Cpl"] < r["Cpu"] else "upper"
def _v(x):
    return f"{x:.1g}" if abs(x) < 0.001 else f"{x:.3g}"

aex_full_gap = float(_vfull.loc[("aex", "hcp"), "r2_minus_pred_r2"])
assert aex_full_gap > max_gap and float(_vfull.loc[("aex", "hcp"), "p_lack_of_fit"]) >= lof_alpha

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- classification evidence (PCMP-001 §6.2 and §7.7, PCP-005 §7 criterion 7)
# an attribute is affected by a parameter when a term of the selected model that contains it is significant
_tp = {r: {term_code(t): float(F[r]["model"].pvalues[t]) for t in F[r]["names"]} for r in RESP}
AFF = {q: {r: {t: p_ for t, p_ in _tp[r].items() if LT[q] in t and p_ < eff_alpha} for r in RESP} for q in FAC}
assert {q: [r for r in RESP if AFF[q][r]] for q in FAC} == {
    "load": ["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "step_yield"], "elution_ph": ["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "lmw_cesds_pct"],
    "flow": ["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "step_yield"], "end_collect": ["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "step_yield"]}
assert _tp["lmw_cesds_pct"]["A"] >= eff_alpha                  # protein load: not significant for fragments
def termp(q, r):
    """The significant terms of output r that contain parameter q, with their p-values, for the text."""
    return join_and([f"{t} ({pf(p_)})" for t, p_ in AFF[q][r].items()])
# the change of pool host cell protein across the NOR-propagated PAR of each parameter, the other parameters at
# their set-points, at manufacturing scale, and the margin of that PAR to the NOR in force
_pmc = D.par_margins(UO).set_index(["response", "factor"])
def par_ends(r, q):
    return float(_pmc.loc[(r, q), "par_low"]), float(_pmc.loc[(r, q), "par_high"])
CLE = {}
for q in FAC:
    lo_, hi_ = par_ends("pool_hcp_ng_mg", q)
    v_ = np.array([hcp_m({q: x}) for x in np.linspace(lo_, hi_, D.PAR_GRID)])
    CLE[q] = dict(v_lo=float(v_[0]), v_hi=float(v_[-1]), span=float(v_.max() - v_.min()),
                  pct=100 * float(v_.max() - v_.min()) / C_HCP,
                  m_lo=float(P[q].nor[0] - lo_), m_hi=float(hi_ - P[q].nor[1]))
    assert CLE[q]["m_lo"] > 0 and CLE[q]["m_hi"] > 0             # every PAR contains the NOR with a margin
# the two critical parameters move pool host cell protein by far more than load flow rate or end of pool collect
assert min(CLE["load"]["pct"], CLE["elution_ph"]["pct"]) > 4 * max(CLE["flow"]["pct"], CLE["end_collect"]["pct"])
assert CLE["load"]["v_hi"] > CLE["load"]["v_lo"] and CLE["elution_ph"]["v_hi"] < CLE["elution_ph"]["v_lo"]
assert CLE["end_collect"]["v_hi"] < CLE["end_collect"]["v_lo"]
assert abs(CLE["elution_ph"]["m_lo"] - par_ph_margin) < 1e-9
assert P["elution_ph"].nor[0] > dev_005_01_ph_measured >= par_ph_lo        # the DEV-005-01 buffer: below the NOR, inside the PAR
# fragments on elution buffer pH, across its PAR for fragments (the range studied)
frag_pct = 100 * frag_eff_B / C_FRAG
assert par(pt, "Fragments", NAMES["elution_ph"]) == rng(P["elution_ph"])      # the fragments PAR is the range studied
frag_ph_m = (float(P["elution_ph"].nor[0] - P["elution_ph"].prange[0]), float(P["elution_ph"].prange[1] - P["elution_ph"].nor[1]))
# step yield, which has no criterion, across the range studied with the other parameters at their set-points
def _yspan(q, **fixed):
    y_ = [100 * float(D.predict(UO, "step_yield", natural={q: [x], **{k: [v] for k, v in fixed.items()}})[0])
          for x in np.linspace(*P[q].prange, D.PAR_GRID)]
    return max(y_) - min(y_)
y_span = {q: _yspan(q) for q in ["load", "end_collect"]}
y_flow_hi = _yspan("flow", load=P["load"].prange[1])            # load flow rate costs yield at high load
y_flow_lo = _yspan("flow", load=P["load"].prange[0])
assert y_flow_hi > 10 * y_flow_lo
# the univariate parameters: the range supported by the individual results, against the NOR
uni_m = {q: (float(P[q].nor[0] - P[q].prange[0]), float(P[q].prange[1] - P[q].nor[1])) for q in ["temperature", "bed_height"]}
assert all(a_ > 0 and b_ > 0 for a_, b_ in uni_m.values())
# DEV-005-02: with the first result in place, the change of leached Protein A across the range of end of pool collect
_c02 = s02["model"].params
s02_chg = float(_bt02(_c02["const"] - _c02["end_collect"]) - _bt02(_c02["const"] + _c02["end_collect"]))
assert 0 < s02_chg < C_LPA / 100
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

This report presents the process characterization of the Protein A chromatography step (Step 5), the capture step of the A-Mab drug substance purification train. It removes most of the host cell protein and DNA of the clarified harvest, and it adds one impurity of its own, Protein A ligand that leaches from the resin. The characterization studies were run under the approved plan PCP-005 in a scale-down model of the commercial column, between `{python} first_start` and `{python} last_end`.

This Version `{python} ver` re-analyses the experiments of Version 1.0 against the criteria of the master plan PCMP-001 Version `{python} ver`, issued under the investigation `{python} INV['id']`. It adds the fragment results by nrCE-SDS and analyses each response-surface output by model selection, as the investigation `{python} INV2['id']` requires. The normal operating ranges (NORs) of the step are not changed.

The step has `{python} n_par` process parameters. Of these, `{python} n_multi` were studied in a `{python} n_scr`-run screening design followed by a `{python} n_rsm`-run response-surface design, and `{python} n_uni` were studied one factor at a time. Protein load and elution buffer pH were classified as well-controlled critical process parameters (WC-CPPs). Load flow rate and end of pool collect were classified as KPPs, and operating temperature and bed height as GPPs. No parameter of the step is in the class CPP.

- F1. The scale-down model is qualified for leached Protein A. Pool host cell protein in the scale-down model is `{python} rt_hcp` times its value at manufacturing scale (`{python} off_ci` % confidence interval `{python} rt_hcp_lo` to `{python} rt_hcp_hi`). Over the NOR in force, with protein load at `{python} nor(P['load'])` g/L resin, the model is not qualified for pool host cell protein. With the ratio at its estimate the upper prediction limit of a single run is `{python} f0(pl_pt)` ng/mg, below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. With the ratio at the low end of its interval it is `{python} f0(pl_lo)` ng/mg, above the criterion. The model is used for pool host cell protein all the same, with the ratio at its estimate (PD-005-10). This holds with every model that the data support about as well as the selected one, on the planned runs alone and against the a priori criterion. The NOR is not narrowed, because NORs come from production. The report flags the protein load NOR for discussion with manufacturing on whether it can be improved. With the ratio at the low end of its interval the limit meets the criterion when the upper edge of the protein load NOR is `{python} f1(load_q_max)` g/L resin. Leached Protein A is `{python} lpa_off` ppm lower in the scale-down model, as expected from the longer hold of the load at manufacturing scale. Fragments were not compared at the two scales (@sec-sdm).
- F2. Each output of the response-surface design was analysed by model selection (PD-005-04), and each selected model meets the adequacy criteria of PCP-005 §7 on lack of fit and predictive power. Pool host cell protein is modelled on the log scale (@sec-stats, @sec-rsm).
- F3. Pool host cell protein rises with protein load and as elution buffer pH falls, by factors of `{python} f2(fac_A)` and `{python} f2(fac_B)` across the ranges studied. The two effects multiply. Whether a further interaction of the two exists on the log scale the data do not decide. Pool host cell protein falls by `{python} f"{fall_D:.0f}"` % as the end of pool collect is extended across its range (@sec-rsm-hcp).
- F4. Step yield rises with end of pool collect and levels off towards the upper end of its range. It falls with protein load, and load flow rate lowers it only at high load (@sec-rsm-yield).
- F5. Leached Protein A does not depend on the `{python} n_fac` parameters of the multivariate design by more than the design resolves. This rests on the re-assay of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` (DEV-005-02). Every run met the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm at manufacturing scale, the highest at `{python} f2(lpa_max_m)` ppm (@sec-rsm-lpa).
- F6. Fragments by nrCE-SDS fall slightly as elution buffer pH rises, by `{python} f2(frag_eff_B)` percentage points across its range studied. All `{python} fr_n` pools of the response-surface design met the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_frag` %, the highest at `{python} f2(fr_max)` % (@sec-rsm-frag).
- F7. Each of the `{python} n_crit` outputs with a criterion met it across the NOR in force, pool host cell protein with the offset ratio at its estimate (F1). The criterion for pool host cell protein, ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, is `{python} f"{widen_pct:.0f}"` % wider than its a priori value, because the one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single batch for the host cell protein clearance of anion exchange is better than its platform worst case. The change is the producer's risk, and an excursion would be detected at release of the drug substance (@sec-par). Every NOR-propagated PAR spans the range studied of its parameter, except that of elution buffer pH for pool host cell protein, `{python} par_ph_hcp`. On the upper prediction limit of a single run, pool host cell protein exceeds its criterion only at high load combined with low pH, never with every parameter inside its NOR (@sec-ds).
- F8. Criterion 5 of PCP-005 §7, on residual trends and influential runs, is met except for leached Protein A and fragments, whose residual trends are small against their criteria (PD-005-02). With each run above `{python} cook_rule` deleted in turn the conclusion over the NOR is the same for every output with a criterion (@sec-resid).
- F9. In a hold study made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis (PD-005-05), one eluate made at set-point was held at elution pH for `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm`. What the hold added kept aggregate, acidic variants and fragments `{python} hold_rule_word` the upper limits of the low-pH inactivation load. Acidic variants can enter the hold below their lower limit of `{python} g(acid_lim[0])` % at the least favourable corner of the production bioreactor NOR, a result of PCR-003, and the hold does not lower them (@sec-hold).
- F10. No difference from the set-point runs was detected in pool host cell protein, step yield or leached Protein A at either end of the ranges of operating temperature and bed height, and each of these results met its criterion. Fragments were not measured by nrCE-SDS in this study (@sec-uni).
- F11. The effect of end of pool collect on pool host cell protein has opposite signs in the screening and the response-surface designs. The difference is larger than the noise of the screening design, and its cause was not identified (@sec-rsm-hcp).

At commercial scale the integrated process model gives a Cpk of `{python} f2(cpk['hcp'])` for host cell protein and `{python} f2(cpk['fragments_lmw'])` for fragments in the drug substance, above the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` of PCMP-001 §7.9. No simulated batch of `{python} f"{n_mc_b:,}"` fell outside the drug substance criterion for host cell protein, leached Protein A, fragments or residual DNA (@sec-cap).

The `{python} n_dev` study events of the step (DEV-005-01 and DEV-005-02) change no judgement of an output against its criterion. The report also records `{python} n_pd` discrepancies from the plan (@sec-dev), and its results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose primary mechanism of action is antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity. It is developed by `{python} COMPANY` and is being transferred from development at the sending site to commercial drug substance manufacture at `{python} scale_l` L scale at the receiving site, under the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001. The drug substance is purified by the platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, small virus retentive filtration and UF/DF.

Protein A chromatography is the first chromatographic step of the purification train. It is operated in bind and elute mode. The resin binds the antibody from the clarified harvest at neutral pH, while host cell protein, DNA and most other components of the feed are removed in the load flow-through and the wash. A low-pH buffer elutes the antibody into a small volume, and the eluate passes to low-pH viral inactivation (Step 6) without neutralization. The step is the principal point of clearance for host cell protein and DNA, and it partly clears fragments. It introduces one attribute of the CQA register, leached Protein A. Although Protein A chromatography removes some virus, no viral clearance claim is made for this step [@amab2009]. The viral clearance claim of the process rests on low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration, and it is consolidated in PCMR-001.

## Objectives

The objectives of the characterization were the following, as PCP-005 §2 states them.

1. Quantify the effect of each characterized parameter on pool host cell protein, on step yield and on leached Protein A, over the ranges given in PCP-005 §6.1.
2. Define the region of the characterized space within which the quality attributes this step controls are predicted to remain within their acceptance criteria.
3. Establish a proven acceptable range for each parameter and each quality attribute the step controls, both with the other parameters at their set-points and with the other parameters varying within their normal operating ranges.
4. Provide the demonstrated effects and the operating region from which each parameter will be classified under SOP-4001.
5. Justify the parameter ranges carried into Stage 2 and the contribution this step makes to the control strategy of the drug substance process.
6. Estimate, before the first characterization run, the offset between the scale-down model and manufacturing scale for each quantity that the qualification compares, and qualify the model by that offset for pool host cell protein and leached Protein A (PCP-005 §5.1).
7. Fit response-surface models for pool host cell protein, step yield, leached Protein A and fragments by nrCE-SDS over the ranges studied, and judge their adequacy for prediction.

Objectives 1 to 5 are those of Version 1.0. Objectives 6 and 7 were added at Version 2.0, which also adds fragments to objectives 1 and 3 and states the ranges of objective 3 at manufacturing scale for pool host cell protein and leached Protein A. Objective 1 is answered in @sec-rsm and @sec-uni, objective 2 in @sec-ds, objective 3 in @sec-par, objective 4 in @sec-class, objective 5 in @sec-par and @sec-cs, objective 6 in @sec-sdm and objective 7 in @sec-rsm.

The hold study of the eluate was not an objective of PCP-005. It was made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis and is recorded as the discrepancy PD-005-05 (@sec-pd05).

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The study is part of Stage 1 (process design) of the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced approach of ICH Q8(R2) and ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq11], in which prior knowledge and risk assessment identify the parameters that may affect quality, and designed experiments then measure and bound those effects. Criticality is treated as a continuum, as ICH Q8(R2) describes it, and risk is managed under ICH Q9 [@ichq9]. The classification of parameters follows the decision logic of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009], as PCMP-001 §7.7 applies it. @tbl-related lists the documents this report depends on and feeds.

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version 1.0 of this report was approved on `{python} rev1_date(DOC)`. Version `{python} ver` takes effect on `{python} eff_date` and is issued under the investigation `{python} INV['id']`. That limit was the drug substance criterion carried back through the nominal downstream clearance of this campaign, then divided by a safety factor of `{python} r1_margin`. The factor was chosen. It was not calculated from how the downstream steps perform (INV-001 finding 2). # Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The same capture step has been used to purify the platform antibodies X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and A-Mab through clinical manufacture [@amab2009]. Staphylococcal Protein A, immobilized on the resin, binds the Fc region of the antibody at the interface between the second and third constant domains of the heavy chain. When the pH is lowered, histidine residues at this interface become protonated, the interaction weakens, and the antibody is released.

Host cell protein reaches the eluate by two routes. Some binds weakly to the resin backbone or to the ligand. Some associates with the antibody through electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions, which the wash does not disrupt while the antibody stays bound to the ligand. This product-associated host cell protein leaves the column with the antibody at any elution pH. A lower elution pH desorbs more of the host cell protein held on the resin, and that protein leaves the column with the product. Pool host cell protein was therefore expected to rise as elution buffer pH falls. In the A-Mab case study pool host cell protein also rose with protein load [@amab2009], and the same direction was expected here. Product-associated host cell protein rises in proportion to the antibody, which leaves the value per mg unchanged. PCP-005 therefore assumed no mechanism for the rise with load (PCP-005 §4.1). The plan expected that the two effects could interact, and both designs can estimate an interaction.

Step yield is lost when antibody breaks through during the load or remains on the column at the end of collection. Breakthrough begins earlier as the load approaches the dynamic binding capacity of the bed. The dynamic binding capacity itself falls as the residence time shortens, because binding is limited by the diffusion of the antibody into the pores of the bead. A higher load flow rate shortens the residence time, which costs yield only when the load is close to the capacity. Yield was therefore expected to fall with flow rate mainly at high load, and to rise as the end of pool collect is extended into the tail of the elution peak.

Leached Protein A comes from hydrolysis of the coupling chemistry and from cleavage of exposed ligand by proteases that the clarified harvest carries into the column. The leached fragments elute with the antibody because they still bind Fc. Leaching is highest on new resin, in its first cycles. A higher protein load or a lower load flow rate lengthens the loading time, and with it the contact of the ligand with the harvest proteases. Leached Protein A is reported per mass of antibody, and if a similar amount of ligand leaches in each cycle the value in ppm falls as protein load rises. PCP-005 expected leached Protein A to depend little on the parameters within their ranges (PCP-005 §4.1).

An antibody fragment that still carries Fc is captured and elutes with the intact antibody. A Fab fragment lacks Fc and is expected to flow through with the load, so the pool is expected to carry less fragment than the feed. Native Protein A also binds the variable domain of heavy chains of the VH3 family, and a Fab fragment of such an antibody can be captured as well. Whether the Fab of A-Mab binds the ligand of this resin was not tested here. A lower elution pH may add a little acid-catalysed hinge hydrolysis during elution. SEC overstates fragments in this matrix, because it reads part of the host cell protein as fragment (INV-001 finding 6). DNA is polyanionic and does not bind Protein A. Its clearance is large and was not expected to depend on the operating parameters within their ranges.

Protein A, when operated under platform conditions, does not separate glycan variants or charge variants, because it binds the Fc region independently of both [@amab2009]. Nor does it separate aggregate from monomer, since both carry Fc. In the Protein A characterization of the case study no process parameter had a significant effect on aggregate [@amab2009]. For these reasons glycan variants, charge variants and aggregate were not responses of the designs.

## Quality attributes in scope

@tbl-cqa lists the attributes in scope of this report with their drug substance criteria and the criticality level the register assigns. Each attribute is a CQA with a level from very low (VL) to very high (VH), assigned with Tool #1, whose score is the product of impact and uncertainty. Acidic variants are in scope because the eluate is held before viral inactivation (@sec-hold).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(cqas_by_keys(["leached_protein_a", "hcp", "fragments_lmw", "residual_dna", "aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants"]).reset_index(drop=True),
        "Quality attributes in scope of this report, with the drug substance criterion and criticality.", "tbl-cqa",
        header={"Acceptance": "Drug substance\ncriterion", "Tool #1": "Tool #1\nscore"},
        align=["P{4.4cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "P{2.8cm}", "c", "c"]).show()
```

The drug substance criteria do not apply to the Protein A pool directly, because cation exchange and anion exchange remove host cell protein, leached Protein A and fragments after this step. Against the drug substance criteria at manufacturing scale, pool host cell protein would fail in all `{python} n_meas['pool_hcp_ng_mg']` results of the designs, leached Protein A in `{python} n_lpa_ds_over` of `{python} n_meas['leached_protein_a_ppm']`, the lowest of them at `{python} f3(lpa_ds_over_min)` ppm, and fragments in none of `{python} n_meas['lmw_cesds_pct']`. Each of these outputs is therefore judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion (@sec-par). Residual DNA has a drug substance criterion but no intermediate acceptance criterion, because the platform history gives no worst-case DNA clearance for the steps after Protein A (PCMP-001 §7.3). It was measured in pg per mg of antibody on the centre points, for information, and it is judged in ng per dose in the drug substance (@sec-cap). The held eluate is judged against the criteria of the low-pH inactivation load (@sec-holddesign). Step yield is a performance attribute without an acceptance criterion, and it is used for the classification of parameters that act on process performance.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

The pre-characterization risk assessment RA-001 assessed every parameter of the step before characterization began. Each parameter was ranked on its potential impact on the CQAs and on process performance, and on its potential to interact with other parameters.

Protein load, elution buffer pH, load flow rate and end of pool collect were assigned to multivariate study. Each carries an effect expected from the mechanism, and the interactions of protein load with elution buffer pH and with load flow rate can only be estimated in a design that varies the parameters together. Operating temperature and bed height were assigned to univariate study. A higher temperature speeds the diffusion of the antibody into the pores, which raises the dynamic binding capacity, and it strengthens the hydrophobic contacts at the Fc–ligand interface, which makes elution slightly less complete. Over the range studied both effects were expected to be small against those of load and pH, and the resin manufacturer specifies binding capacity across that range. Bed height is held by the packing specification in manufacture, and at constant linear velocity it sets the residence time.

The ranges studied are between `{python} f'{wr_min:.1f}'` and `{python} f'{wr_max:.1f}'` times the width of the NOR. They bound the knowledge space within which a PAR can be claimed. Load flow rate is set as a linear velocity, so at the set-point bed height it fixes the residence time. The residence time is `{python} g(rt_set)` min at the set-point flow rate, and over the range studied it runs from `{python} g(rt_hi)` min at the highest flow to `{python} g(rt_lo)` min at the lowest. The upper end of the flow range therefore tests the shortest residence time, the condition most likely to cause breakthrough at high load, and the two ends of the elution pH range test the strongest and the weakest elution.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The scale-down model is a laboratory column packed with the commercial Protein A resin and operated under SOP-2007 on the scaling principles of PCMP-001 §5. The bed height and the residence time of the commercial column were kept. Load, wash and elution volumes were normalized to column volumes, and buffers were made to the commercial recipes. Column efficiency was checked by plate count and peak asymmetry after packing. PCP-005 sets no criterion for either, and both are reported for information.

The model was qualified under SOP-1001 by its offset from manufacturing scale, the rule of PCMP-001 §7.1 that PCP-005 §5.1 applies to this step. Set-point runs of the scale-down model were compared with `{python} n_m` manufacturing-scale batches of A-Mab run at set-point. The outputs compared were pool host cell protein, leached Protein A, step yield, and column efficiency as plates per metre and peak asymmetry. The offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches, with its two-sided `{python} off_ci` % confidence interval from a Student t interval with pooled variance. It is taken on the scale on which the output is modelled (@sec-stats). Pool host cell protein is modelled on the log scale. Its offset is therefore the difference of the mean logarithms, reported as the ratio of the geometric means of the two scales, a multiplicative offset. A scale-down result of pool host cell protein is divided by this ratio before it is judged against a criterion, and a result of leached Protein A has its offset subtracted. Every range and every conclusion for these two outputs is therefore at manufacturing scale.

The model is qualified for an output when the conclusion against its criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its confidence interval. That conclusion is whether the output meets its criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the `{python} n_fac` response-surface factors, judged on the upper prediction limit of a single run (@sec-stats). Step yield and column efficiency have no criterion at the step. Their offsets are recorded, and no conclusion depends on them.

@tbl-sdm-offsets gives the offsets over all `{python} n_sd_all` scale-down runs, with `{python} off_df` degrees of freedom. Of these, `{python} n_sd_plan` were planned in study S-PA-SDM (`{python} win('S-PA-SDM')`), before the first run of the screening design, and `{python} n_sd_supp` were made in study S-PA-SDM2 (`{python} win('S-PA-SDM2')`) during the Version 2.0 re-analysis (discrepancy PD-005-01, @sec-pd01).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets(["protein_a"]).show()
```

Pool host cell protein in the scale-down model is `{python} rt_hcp` times its value at manufacturing scale. The `{python} off_ci` % confidence interval of this ratio, `{python} rt_hcp_lo` to `{python} rt_hcp_hi`, `{python} 'includes' if hcp_ci_one else 'excludes'` 1. Dividing by the low end of the interval raises each prediction most, so the low end is the unfavourable end for an upper criterion.

Over the NOR in force, with protein load at `{python} nor(P['load'])` g/L resin, the scale-down model is not qualified for pool host cell protein. The upper prediction limit of a single run over the NOR is `{python} f0(pl_pt)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale with the ratio at its estimate and `{python} f0(pl_hi)` ng/mg with the ratio at its high end, both below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. With the ratio at its low end it is `{python} f0(pl_lo)` ng/mg, above the criterion. The conclusion therefore changes across the interval of the ratio. With the other factors over their NORs, the limit at the low end of the ratio meets the criterion when the upper edge of the protein load NOR is `{python} f1(load_q_max)` g/L resin.

The NOR is not narrowed. NORs come from production. An offset compares laboratory results with production scale, so it can change a PAR but not a NOR. No NOR of the step lies outside its NOR-propagated PAR at manufacturing scale (@sec-par). The flag of this report therefore comes from the qualification of the scale-down model and not from a PAR. The report flags the protein load NOR for discussion with manufacturing on whether it can be improved. The load of `{python} f1(load_q_max)` g/L resin is the information that discussion needs.

PCMP-001 §5 asks the report to state the consequence. Every judgement of pool host cell protein in this report is made with the ratio at its estimate, as PCMP-001 §7.1 rule 2 requires, and on that basis pool host cell protein meets its criterion across the NOR in force. The study does not show that this holds over the whole interval of the ratio. At the upper end of the protein load NOR, a true ratio near the low end of its interval would put the upper prediction limit of a single run above the criterion. The judgements over the NOR, the design space and the PARs for pool host cell protein carry this limitation. PCMP-001 §7.1 states that "a model whose conclusion for an output changes between the two ends of the offset interval is not used for that output". This report uses the model of pool host cell protein all the same, and that departure is the discrepancy PD-005-10 (@sec-pd10).

The conclusion does not depend on the choices behind the analysis.

1. The criterion. Without the model selection of `{python} INV2['id']` corrective action CA3 the criterion would be its a priori value of ≤ `{python} f0(crit_wo)` ng/mg (@sec-par). Against it the model is not qualified either. The limit with the ratio at its estimate, `{python} f0(pl_pt)` ng/mg, is below that criterion, and the limit with the ratio at its low end, `{python} f0(pl_lo)` ng/mg, is above it.
2. The added runs. On the `{python} n_sd_plan` planned runs alone the interval of the ratio is wider, and the model is not qualified either (@sec-pd01).
3. The model. Each of the `{python} n_near` models whose AICc lies within 2 units of that of the selected model gives a limit above the criterion with the ratio at its low end (@sec-rsm-hcp).

Leached Protein A is `{python} lpa_off` ppm lower in the scale-down model. The `{python} off_ci` % confidence interval of the difference, `{python} lpa_off_a` to `{python} lpa_off_b` ppm lower, excludes zero, and each scale-down run was below the manufacturing mean. The expected cause is cleavage of the ligand by harvest proteases. At manufacturing scale the clarified harvest is held longer before capture. Proteolytic activity in the harvest is expected to rise while it is held, and the load then cleaves more ligand from the resin during loading. This study does not test that cause. With the offset at either end of its interval the conclusion for leached Protein A is the same, and the model is qualified for it. On the `{python} n_sd_plan` runs of the planned study S-PA-SDM alone, the two scales differ in leached Protein A (`{python} pf(dev04_p)`). PCP-005 Version 1.0 required such a difference to be investigated before the characterization studies, and it was not (discrepancy PD-005-08, @sec-pd08).

Fragments by nrCE-SDS were not compared at the two scales. The method decision AMD-001 of `{python} AMD['date']`, which set nrCE-SDS as the method for fragments at every step, was taken after study S-PA-SDM had closed. The `{python} n_sd_supp` runs of study S-PA-SDM2 were made after AMD-001 and were not tested by nrCE-SDS either. Fragments therefore have no measured offset (PCMP-001 §7.1), and their conclusions assume no difference between the scales. The scale-down model is accepted for fragments on mechanism, as PCP-005 §5.1 states. The capture of Fc-bearing species depends on bed height and residence time, and low-pH hinge hydrolysis on pH, time and temperature, all of which the model keeps at commercial values.

The longer hold of the load at manufacturing scale could also raise fragments, because the harvest proteases that cleave the ligand can also clip the antibody. The hold study of the clarified harvest (PCR-004) bounds this effect. Over `{python} hh_days` days fragments by nrCE-SDS in the clarified harvest rose by at most `{python} f2(hh_inc_max)` percentage points, at `{python} hh_t`. Suppose the longer hold added that much fragment to the pool, every fragment it formed being captured. The upper prediction limit of fragments over the NOR, `{python} f2(frag_nor_up)` %, would then become `{python} f2(frag_with_hold)` %, still below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_frag` %. This bound holds for a hold of the clarified harvest within the `{python} hh_days` days of that study. The hold study of the eluate measured attributes that the qualification did not compare, so its results also carry no offset.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

Each run followed SOP-2007 at laboratory scale. The column was equilibrated, loaded with clarified harvest to the target protein load, washed, and eluted with the elution buffer at the pH set by the design. The protein load of each run was set from the load volume and the titre of the clarified harvest by Protein A affinity HPLC (AMV-3021, under SOP-3016). The eluate was collected from the rise of the absorbance at 280 nm until the end of pool collect set by the design, in column volumes. The column was then stripped, cleaned and stored under SOP-2008. The pool was not neutralized, because the commercial eluate passes to low-pH viral inactivation at elution pH.

Each design was loaded from one pool of clarified harvest produced at set-point and held frozen in aliquots. A single feed keeps feed variation out of the estimated effects. The effect of feed quality on the step was therefore not estimated in these studies. The case study reports that Protein A capture is robust over a wide range of feed inputs [@amab2009], and the feed is characterized in PCR-003 and PCR-004. Runs were executed in random order within each design. The resin was used within the life-cycle limits of SOP-2008, and the life cycle of the resin is outside the scope of this report.

## Analytical methods {#sec-methods}

Each response was measured by a validated method under its own AMV. @tbl-sops lists the controlled procedures and method validations used. The SOP and AMV numbers are placeholders.


Pool host cell protein was measured by ELISA (AMV-3012) and is reported per mass of antibody in the pool, so that it does not depend on how far the pool is diluted by the end of pool collect. The precision of the ELISA is `{python} g(elisa_prec)` % of the level. The titre of the clarified harvest was measured by Protein A affinity HPLC (AMV-3021, under SOP-3016), which measures the antibody alone, with a precision of `{python} g(titre_prec)` %. Step yield is the mass of antibody in the pool, from the protein concentration by absorbance at 280 nm (AMV-3019) and the pool volume, divided by the mass loaded, from the titre and the load volume. PCP-005 §5.3 planned both masses by absorbance at 280 nm, so the titre basis of the loaded mass is the discrepancy PD-005-06. In the pool, host cell protein is at most `{python} f1(hcp_frac_max)` % of the mass of antibody, so the absorbance at 280 nm there is mainly that of the antibody. Leached Protein A was measured by ELISA (AMV-3016). Fragments were measured by nrCE-SDS (AMV-3020, under SOP-3015), as PCMP-001 §7.8 sets for every step. SEC (AMV-3011) remains the method for aggregate (PCMP-001 §7.8). Acidic variants in the hold study were measured by icIEF (AMV-3013), and residual DNA by qPCR (AMV-3014). @tbl-methods-by-study shows which method measured fragments in each study of the step, and Appendix D summarizes the methods.

The screening design ran before the method decision AMD-001 set nrCE-SDS as the method for fragments, and its pools were not retained. Its fragment results are by SEC only and are not used for any decision. The univariate study S-PA-UNI ran before AMD-001, and its samples were not retained, so its fragment results are by SEC only and are not used for any decision.
