On those pools SEC read fragments higher than nrCE-SDS by `{python} f2(sec_minus.min())` to `{python} f2(sec_minus.max())` percentage points (median `{python} f2(sec_minus.median())`). The hold study ran after AMD-001 and measured fragments by nrCE-SDS alone.

## Sampling plan

The load of each design was sampled once per feed aliquot thawed. The pool of every run was sampled once at the end of collection, after mixing, and its volume was recorded. Each pool sample was divided into aliquots for each method. One further aliquot of every response-surface pool was retained frozen under the sample management procedure of Analytical Development, and these are the samples tested by nrCE-SDS in study S-PA-RET. The screening design had `{python} cp_scr` centre points and the response-surface design `{python} cp_rsm`. Residual DNA was measured on the load and pool of the centre-point runs. The hold study was sampled as described in @sec-holddesign.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

The designs were built and analysed under SOP-1002 with the common approach of PCMP-001 §6. Factors were coded from −1 to +1 over their range studied, with 0 at the centre. For each of the `{python} n_fac` design factors the centre of the range studied is the set-point, so the centre-point runs of both designs are set-point runs. In this report a term of a model is a main effect, an interaction or a square, and the intercept is counted apart.

The screening data were fitted with a model of main effects and two-factor interactions. Effects are reported as the change in the response over the coded range of the factor, which is twice the coefficient. Significance was judged at α = `{python} g(eff_alpha)`. The screening model identifies effects. A two-level design cannot resolve curvature, so the screening model was not used to predict between its corners.

PCP-005 §5.5 planned to fit the full quadratic model, an intercept and `{python} n_terms_full` terms, to each output of the response-surface design. Each output was analysed instead by model selection, which `{python} INV2['id']` introduced as its corrective action CA3 on `{python} ca3_date` for every report with a response-surface design. PCMP-001 Version 2.0 still names the full quadratic model, so the selection is a discrepancy from the plan, recorded as PD-005-04 (@sec-dev). The selection first chooses the scale of each output and then the terms of its model. Pool host cell protein is the one output put on the log scale, and both choices are explained below with its data.

### The scale of the model

On the raw scale a model describes pool host cell protein in ng/mg as a sum, $y = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + \dots + \varepsilon$, where $x_1$ is a coded parameter, $b_1$ its coefficient and $\varepsilon$ the run-to-run error. Each parameter then adds or removes a fixed amount, and the error is a fixed amount too. On the log scale the model is $\ln y = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + \dots + \varepsilon$. Transformed back, $y = e^{b_0} \cdot e^{b_1 x_1} \cdots e^{\varepsilon}$, so each parameter multiplies pool host cell protein by a fixed factor. The factor is $e^{b}$ per coded unit and $e^{2b}$ from the low to the high end of the range studied. The run-to-run error multiplies the output as well, so its size in ng/mg grows with the level. In the selected model pool host cell protein rises by a factor of `{python} f2(fac_A)` from the low to the high end of protein load, falls by a factor of `{python} f2(fac_B)` from the low to the high end of elution buffer pH, and falls to `{python} f2(fac_D)` times its value over the range of end of pool collect.

Two properties of this output make a factor the natural description. A purification step removes a share of what is present, so a parameter that changes the performance of the step changes the share of host cell protein that reaches the pool, not a fixed amount. The precision of the host cell protein ELISA is a percentage of the level, `{python} g(elisa_prec)` % (AMV-3012), so the scatter of the results grows with their level.

Least squares, and the t-tests, F-tests and prediction intervals built on it, assume that the residuals are independent and normally distributed, with mean zero and the same variance over the whole range studied. On the raw scale the residuals of pool host cell protein do not have the same variance. In the full quadratic model on the raw scale, their root mean square is `{python} f0(raw_lo)` ng/mg in the lower half of the predicted values and `{python} f0(raw_hi)` ng/mg in the upper half, `{python} f"{raw_ratio:.0f}"` % larger. In the full quadratic model on the log scale the two halves give `{python} f3(log_lo)` and `{python} f3(log_hi)` in natural-log units, `{python} f"{log_ratio:.0f}"` % apart, so the variance is about constant. The Box-Cox profile of the full quadratic model [@boxcox1964] points the same way. Its estimate of the exponent λ is `{python} f2(bc['lambda'])`, and its 95 % interval, `{python} mn(f2(bc['lo']))` to `{python} f2(bc['hi'])`, contains 0, the log scale, and excludes 1, the raw scale. The rule of the selection puts an output on the log scale exactly when this interval contains 0 and excludes 1. For step yield, leached Protein A and fragments the interval contains 1, and these outputs stay on the raw scale. The residual plot of the selected model shows no funnel (@fig-diag-hcp).

The log scale changes how results are read, not what is judged. The criterion stays in ng/mg. Effects are fold changes. The scale-down offset of pool host cell protein is a ratio of geometric means, and a scale-down prediction is divided by it (@sec-sdm). A prediction interval is calculated on the log scale and transformed back. It keeps its 95 % coverage, because the probability that $\ln y$ lies between two values is the probability that $y$ lies between their antilogarithms. It is therefore suitable, and on the log scale the assumption of least squares holds, which on the raw scale it does not. The interval is asymmetric, further above the predicted value than below it. At the set-point the predicted value is `{python} f0(sp_med)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale, and the 95 % prediction interval of a single run runs from `{python} f0(sp_lo)` to `{python} f0(sp_hi)` ng/mg, `{python} f0(sp_med - sp_lo)` below and `{python} f0(sp_hi - sp_med)` above. The predicted value is the median of pool host cell protein, its geometric mean, not its arithmetic mean. The upper prediction limit, which decides against an upper criterion, does not depend on that distinction. Near an upper criterion, where the level is high, a model on the raw scale understates the scatter, because its residual standard deviation is pooled over all levels. The interval from the log scale is wider there, as the data require.

### The terms of the model

The terms were then chosen by a search with one goal, the model with the lowest AICc among all hierarchical submodels of the full quadratic model. A hierarchical model contains an interaction only with both of its main effects, and a square only with its main effect. AICc, Akaike's information criterion with the correction for small samples [@hurvich1989; @burnham2002], estimates how well a model would predict new runs. It rewards the fit and penalises every estimated parameter, and it counts the residual variance as one of them. Its correction raises the penalty when the runs are few for the number of parameters, as in a design of `{python} n_rsm` runs, so that the criterion does not favour too many terms. Every candidate was fitted, `{python} f"{n_cand:,}"` hierarchical models for `{python} n_fac` factors, and the one with the lowest AICc was taken.

A stepwise search, which adds or removes one term at a time, stops when no single change lowers AICc. It can therefore stop at a model that only a combination of changes would improve. On the data of this campaign a stepwise search by AICc would have stopped at a model with a higher AICc for `{python} n_sc_worse` of the `{python} n_sc` outputs that have a criterion and an AICc. At this step a search forward from the mean would have stopped at `{python} sw_hcp_fwd` terms for pool host cell protein. A search backward from the full quadratic model would have stopped at `{python} sw_lpa_bwd` terms for leached Protein A and `{python} sw_frag_bwd` for fragments, each with a higher AICc than the selected model. The backward elimination of `{python} INV2['id']` corrective action CA2 differed in three ways. It was stepwise, it removed terms by p-value, a test of each term against zero and not a comparison of models, and it used the raw scale only. For fragments it kept `{python} join_and([tname(t) for t in ca2_frag])` alone, where the search keeps `{python} join_and([tname(t) for t in fF['names']])`.

The selected model was then judged against the model adequacy criteria of PCP-005 §7 listed below. A model with no term has no F-test, and criterion 2 does not apply to it. Such a model shows that, within the range studied, the output does not depend on the parameters by more than the variation of the runs can resolve. Finally, the scale-down offset of each output was taken on the scale of its model.

### Adequacy, prediction and ranges

Each model is reported with R², adjusted R², predicted R² (from PRESS) [@montgomery2017], the model F-test, and the test of lack of fit against pure error from the centre points. Coefficients are reported in coded units, so that each measures the change in the response over half the range studied, in natural-log units for a log-scale model. The adequacy criteria of PCP-005 §7 were applied as follows. The numbers are those of PCP-005 §7, where criterion 1 is the qualification of the scale-down model (@sec-sdm).

2. Model significance. The model F-test is significant at α = `{python} g(eff_alpha)`.
3. Lack of fit. The lack of fit test is not significant at α = `{python} g(lof_alpha)`.
4. Predictive power. Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} f2(max_gap)`. PCMP-001 §7.2 compares predicted R² with R², not with adjusted R².
5. Residuals. Regressions of the absolute residuals on the predicted values, and of the residuals on run order, show no slope significant at α = `{python} g(res_alpha)`. A run with a Cook's distance above `{python} cook_rule` (`{python} f2(cook_lim)` for `{python} n_rsm` runs) is examined by deleting it and repeating the judgement. The model fails the criterion only where a run's Cook's distance exceeds the `{python} f_q_word` of the F distribution with p and n − p degrees of freedom, p being the number of coefficients of the model.

PCMP-001 §7.2 provides that a model that fails the lack of fit test, or whose predicted R² falls short of R² by more than `{python} f2(max_gap)`, is refitted with a justified change of terms or transformation, or is not used to set a range.

Each output with a criterion is judged over the NOR at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the `{python} n_fac` response-surface factors. The value compared with the criterion is the upper end of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run, which includes the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients and the residual. The criteria of this step are upper limits, so only that end is compared, which makes it a one-sided 97.5 % prediction limit (PCP-005 §7). This report calls it the upper prediction limit.

The PAR analysis follows PCMP-001 §6.4. The univariate PAR, which PCP-005 §8.2 calls the set-point analysis, holds the other parameters at their set-points. It is judged on the prediction of the model, the median for pool host cell protein and the mean for the other outputs. The NOR-propagated PAR is a multivariate PAR. It is the range of a parameter over which a single batch meets the criterion while the other parameters vary within their NORs. It is computed by Monte Carlo at `{python} D.PAR_GRID` grid points across the range studied, with `{python} f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"` operating points at each. Each other parameter is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation of one sixth of its NOR, clipped to its range studied, and the coefficients of the model are drawn from their estimated covariance together with the residual. At each grid point the 97.5th percentile of the simulated batches must meet an upper criterion, so that at least 97.5 % of them meet it. The NOR-propagated PAR is the one that supports a PAR carried into the control strategy. The design space is drawn on the 95 % prediction interval of a single run, on a grid of `{python} DS_N` points per factor over the range studied (@sec-ds).

For each output with a criterion, each run with a Cook's distance above `{python} cook_rule` was deleted in turn, the model selection repeated and the output judged over the NOR again, as criterion 5 requires. Where a selected model does not meet criterion 5, the size of each residual trend is stated against the criterion of its output, and the use of that model for the ranges and the design space is the discrepancy PD-005-02 (@sec-resid).

Capability at commercial scale was estimated from the integrated process model of the train, which runs `{python} mc_n` simulated batches with each parameter drawn within its NOR. Capability is reported as Cpk against the drug substance criterion, one-sided for a criterion with one limit and the lower of the two one-sided indices for a two-sided criterion. It is judged against the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` and the minimum of `{python} f2(CPK_MIN)` of PCMP-001 §7.9. The same simulation counts the batches outside each drug substance criterion. Where none falls outside, the probability of an out-of-specification batch in the simulation is bounded by the one-sided `{python} f"{100 * conf:.0f}"` % upper confidence limit of a proportion with no event in `{python} mc_n` trials.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

@tbl-params lists the parameters of the step with their set-point, NOR, range studied, classification and study type.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rp = rp.reset_index(drop=True).assign(**{"Set-point": rp["Set-point"].map(g).values}).rename(columns={"Char. range": "Range studied"})
_ld = _rp["Parameter"] == P["load"].name
assert _ld.sum() == 1 and _rp.loc[_ld, "NOR"].iloc[0] == nor(P["load"])
_rp.loc[_ld, "NOR"] = _rp.loc[_ld, "NOR"] + "^a)^"
_rp_notes = [("a)", "Over this NOR the scale-down model is not qualified for pool HCP. The NOR is not narrowed, and it is "
                    "flagged for discussion with manufacturing.")]
T.frame(_rp, "Parameters of the Protein A step with set-point, NOR, range studied, classification and study type.", "tbl-params",
        header={"Set-point": "Set-\npoint", "Range studied": "Range\nstudied"}, align=["P{3.6cm}", "P{1.9cm}", "c", "c", "c", "l", "l"],
        notes=_rp_notes).show()
```

The execution window of every study of the step is recorded in @tbl-chronology. Each study began after PCP-005 Version 1.0 was approved on `{python} plan_appr`. Study S-PA-UNI ran before the response-surface design began, against the order of PCP-005 §11, in which the univariate assessments come fourth (discrepancy PD-005-09, @sec-pd09).

_ch = chron.reset_index().sort_values("start")[["id", "kind", "start", "end"]].rename(columns={"id": "Study", "kind": "Study type", "start": "Start", "end": "End"})
_ch["Study type"] = _ch["Study type"].map(lambda k: STUDY_TYPE.get(k, k))

## Screening design

The screening design (study S-PA-SCR, `{python} win('S-PA-SCR')`) was a full two-level factorial design in the `{python} n_fac` factors, with `{python} n_fact` factorial runs and `{python} cp_scr` centre points, `{python} n_scr` runs in all. In a full factorial no effect is aliased with another, and every main effect and every two-factor interaction can be estimated. The responses were pool host cell protein, step yield and leached Protein A, with fragments by SEC recorded for information. All `{python} n_fac` factors were carried into the response-surface design whatever the screening result, as PCP-005 §6.2 planned. Appendix A gives the matrix and the results.

@tbl-legend gives the letter code of each design factor, which the coefficient tables and the appendices use.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(D.factor_legend_df(UO).drop(columns=["Studied in"]), "Letter codes of the design factors.", "tbl-legend",
        align=["c", "l", "l"]).show()
```

## Response-surface design

The response-surface design (study S-PA-RSM, `{python} win('S-PA-RSM')`) was a face-centred central composite design in the same `{python} n_fac` factors. It has `{python} n_fact` factorial runs, `{python} n_axial` axial runs at the faces of the cube and `{python} cp_rsm` centre points, `{python} n_rsm` runs in all. The full quadratic model, an intercept and `{python} n_terms_full` terms, would leave `{python} int(fH['full']['model'].df_resid)` residual degrees of freedom, with `{python} fH['full']['df_pe']` for pure error and `{python} fH['full']['df_lof']` for lack of fit. The responses were pool host cell protein, step yield, leached Protein A and fragments by nrCE-SDS on the retained pools. Appendix B gives the matrix and the results.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-uni-design}

Operating temperature and bed height were studied one factor at a time in the univariate study S-PA-UNI (`{python} win('S-PA-UNI')`), with the other parameters at their set-points. Each was run `{python} uni_reps` times at the low and the high end of its range studied. The `{python} uni_n_ref` set-point runs of the planned qualification study S-PA-SDM served as the reference, in place of the runs at the centre of each range that PCP-005 §6.4 requires (discrepancy PD-005-07, @sec-pd07). Bed height was varied at the set-point linear velocity, so that the residence time changed with it. The shortest bed gives a residence time of `{python} g(rt_short)` min, shorter than any run of the designs. As PCP-005 §6.4 requires, the responses were those of the multivariate designs, pool host cell protein, step yield and leached Protein A, with aggregate and fragments by SEC. Fragments were not measured by nrCE-SDS (@sec-methods). For pool host cell protein and leached Protein A, the range of operating temperature or of bed height is supported when every individual result at both ends meets its criterion at manufacturing scale (PCP-005 §6.4). A univariate study cannot detect an interaction. The ranges of these two parameters are therefore supported only with the other parameters at their set-points.

## Hold study of the Protein A eluate {#sec-holddesign}

The Protein A eluate is held at elution pH before viral inactivation. The hold study S-PA-HLD (`{python} win('S-PA-HLD')`) was made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis, after INV-001 closed, and is recorded as the discrepancy PD-005-05 (@sec-pd05). One eluate was produced at set-point, with elution buffer pH `{python} g(hold_ph)`, divided and held at `{python} t_cold` and `{python} t_warm` for up to `{python} h_days` days. Samples were taken on days `{python} h_daylist` at each temperature, and aggregate by SEC, acidic variants by icIEF and fragments by nrCE-SDS were measured at every sample point.

The plan set no hold criterion, because it foresaw no hold study. The held eluate is the load of low-pH viral inactivation, so it is judged against the intermediate acceptance criteria in force for that load, as the verification of PCMP-001 §7.5 left them, and not against their a priori values. For aggregate and acidic variants they equal the criteria of the production bioreactor output, because capture is expected to leave both unchanged (@sec-prior), and for fragments that of the Protein A pool. This report does not test the expectation for aggregate and acidic variants, because neither was measured in the load of this step. For aggregate the criterion is ≤ `{python} agg_crit` % HMW. It is the drug substance limit of `{python} agg_ds` % less the aggregate increase of UF/DF, `{python} f3(v_ufdf_agg['predicted_nor_bound95'])` percentage points, multiplied by the aggregate clearance of cation exchange, `{python} f3(v_cex_agg['predicted_nor_bound95'])`-fold, less the aggregate increase of low-pH viral inactivation, `{python} f3(v_vi_agg['predicted_nor_bound95'])` percentage points. Each value is the one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single batch of its step, which replaced a platform worst case (PCMP-001 §7.5). PCMP-001 assumed that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate. UF/DF raises it within its NOR, which made the criterion stricter. Cation exchange cleared less aggregate within its NOR than its platform worst case of `{python} f2(v_cex_agg['assumed'])`-fold, which made the criterion stricter. Low-pH viral inactivation added less aggregate than its platform worst case of `{python} f2(v_vi_agg['assumed'])` points, which made it wider. The net change, from ≤ `{python} agg_apri` % a priori to ≤ `{python} agg_crit` %, makes the criterion stricter. The platform aggregate increase was measured over a hold of `{python} vi_plat_min` min, the longest hold studied at low pH, and the A-Mab bound within the hold-time NOR as characterized, which ends at `{python} vi_hold_max` min. The bound is smaller because the A-Mab hold is shorter, not because the product is more stable. At the edges of the range studied A-Mab added up to `{python} f2(v_vi_agg['observed_edge'])` points of aggregate, more than the platform value of `{python} f2(v_vi_agg['assumed'])`, and within the NOR at most `{python} f2(v_vi_agg['predicted_nor'])` points. The aggregate criterion is still right, because routine manufacture does not hold longer than the NOR.

For acidic variants the criterion is `{python} acid_crit` %, its a priori value. Its upper limit is the drug substance limit of `{python} acid_ds_hi` % less the platform worst case of the increase in low-pH viral inactivation, `{python} f2(v_vi_acid['assumed'])` percentage points (@sec-par), and its lower limit is that of the drug substance. Fragments are judged against the intermediate acceptance criterion of the pool, ≤ `{python} crit_frag` % by nrCE-SDS.

Against these criteria the report judges what the hold adds to the eluate, by a hold rule of its own that is part of the discrepancy PD-005-05. A hold time is supported at a temperature when the largest increase from day 0 up to that time, added to the highest level expected in the Protein A pool in manufacture, stays within its criterion. For aggregate and acidic variants the highest level expected is the upper prediction limit of the production bioreactor model over its NOR (PCR-003), and for fragments that of the fragment model of this step, `{python} f2(frag_nor_up)` % (@sec-rsm-frag). Acidic variants are also judged against their lower limit (INV-001 finding 4).

# Results

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility

The centre points of each design were run at set-point and estimate the pure error against which lack of fit is tested. @tbl-cp-rsm gives their mean, standard deviation and coefficient of variation in the response-surface design, and @tbl-cp-scr in the screening design. Fragments by nrCE-SDS were measured in the response-surface design only.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(cp_rsm_df, "Centre-point reproducibility in the response-surface design.", "tbl-cp-rsm",
        align=["P{4.0cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r"]).show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(cp_df("screening"), "Centre-point reproducibility in the screening design.", "tbl-cp-scr",
        align=["P{4.0cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r"]).show()
```

Step yield was the most reproducible response, with a coefficient of variation of `{python} f1(cv_r.loc[L['step_yield'], '%CV'])` % in the response-surface design. Pool host cell protein reproduced to `{python} f1(cv_r.loc[L['pool_hcp_ng_mg'], '%CV'])` % in the response-surface design and to `{python} f1(cv_s.loc[L['pool_hcp_ng_mg'], '%CV'])` % in the screening design. The larger screening value makes the screening tests for pool host cell protein less sensitive than those of the response-surface design. Fragments by nrCE-SDS reproduced to `{python} f1(cpf_cv)` %. Leached Protein A was the least precise response, at `{python} f1(cv_r.loc[L['leached_protein_a_ppm'], '%CV'])` % in the response-surface design. Its standard deviation at the centre points, `{python} f2(lpa_cp_sd)` ppm, is `{python} f"{lpa_cp_ratio:.0f}"` % larger than its standard deviation across all `{python} n_rsm` runs of the design, `{python} f2(lpa_all_sd)` ppm. With pure error this large against the variation between runs, the lack of fit test of leached Protein A has little power.

## Screening: factor effects

@tbl-scr-fit summarizes the screening models. The models for pool host cell protein and step yield are significant. The model for leached Protein A is not (`{python} pf(scr_fit.loc[L['leached_protein_a_ppm'], 'p-value'])`), and none of its terms is significant.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(scr_fit_df(), "Screening model summary (main effects and two-factor interactions).", "tbl-scr-fit",
        align=["P{4.0cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "RMSE, root mean square error, for step yield in percentage points.")]).show()
```

Pool host cell protein was affected by elution buffer pH (B) and protein load (A). Raising the elution pH across its range lowered pool host cell protein by `{python} f0(abs(eH['B']['Effect']))` ng/mg, and raising protein load across its range raised it by `{python} f0(eH['A']['Effect'])` ng/mg. In ng/mg the screening model also shows an interaction of protein load with elution buffer pH (AB, `{python} mn(f0(eH['AB']['Effect']))` ng/mg, `{python} pf(eH['AB']['p-value'])`), so the fall with rising pH is larger at high load. Two effects that multiply produce an interaction of this sign in ng/mg, and the response-surface analysis examines it on the log scale (@sec-rsm-hcp). Load flow rate and end of pool collect had no significant effect in the screening design (@tbl-scr-hcp).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(eff_df("pool_hcp_ng_mg"), "Screening effects on pool HCP (ng/mg), sorted by size.", "tbl-scr-hcp", align="lrrrrr").show()
```

Step yield was affected by end of pool collect (D), protein load (A) and load flow rate (C), and by the interaction of protein load with load flow rate (AC). Extending the end of pool collect across its range raised yield by `{python} f1(100 * eY['D']['Effect'])` percentage points. Raising protein load and load flow rate lowered it by `{python} f1(100 * abs(eY['A']['Effect']))` and `{python} f1(100 * abs(eY['C']['Effect']))` percentage points. The interaction of protein load with load flow rate (`{python} mn(f1(100 * eY['AC']['Effect']))` percentage points, `{python} pf(eY['AC']['p-value'])`) means that flow rate costs more yield at high load. The interactions of load flow rate with end of pool collect (CD) and of elution buffer pH with end of pool collect (BD) were also significant, at `{python} mn(f1(100 * eY['CD']['Effect']))` and `{python} mn(f1(100 * eY['BD']['Effect']))` percentage points. They are smaller than the significant main effects, and neither is in the model selected for step yield in the response-surface design. The p-value of BD, `{python} f3(bd_p)`, rests on the unrounded results. Refitted from the yields as Appendix A prints them, to 0.1 %, it is `{python} f3(bd_p_round)`. Elution buffer pH had no significant effect on yield. @tbl-scr-yield gives the effects, and Appendix C gives the effects for leached Protein A.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(eff_df("step_yield", k=100, nd=2), "Screening effects on step yield (percentage points), sorted by size.", "tbl-scr-yield",
        align="lrrrrr", notes=[("", "Computed from the unrounded results. Appendix A prints step yield to 0.1 %.")]).show()
```

The screening results agree in direction with the expectations of @sec-prior for protein load and elution buffer pH on pool host cell protein, and for protein load, load flow rate, their interaction and end of pool collect on step yield.

## Response-surface models {#sec-rsm}

Each output of the response-surface design was analysed by the model selection of @sec-stats. Under the rule of the investigation `{python} INV2['id']` for planned models that failed PCMP-001 §7.2, no runs were added to the Protein A design. Leached Protein A showed no effect to resolve, and for fragments no second block within the size of the planned design reached the assurance of at least `{python} f2(assurance)` that `{python} INV2['id']` requires. Every run of the design is therefore in one block. @tbl-reeval-protein-a compares the full quadratic model that PCP-005 planned, fitted to the `{python} n_rsm` planned runs, with the model selected for each output with a criterion.

In the full quadratic model the predicted R² of leached Protein A and of fragments is below zero. Both fail by a wide margin the limit of PCMP-001 §7.2 that predicted R² may fall no more than `{python} f2(max_gap)` below R². For pool host cell protein the full quadratic model on the raw scale, with run `{python} dev_run` at its recorded pH, fails the lack of fit test (`{python} pf(p_lof_raw_full)`). With run `{python} dev_run` at its design pH, as Version 1.0 and `{python} INV2['id']` fitted it, the same model meets both tests, with a gap of `{python} f3(fv1_gap)` and a lack of fit test of `{python} pf(fv1_plof)`. The full quadratic model of step yield, which has no criterion and is not in the table, also fails the limit, with predicted R² `{python} f2(fY_full_gap)` below R².

```{python}
#| output: asis
_re = T.model_reevaluation("protein_a")
_re.notes = list(_re.notes) + [("", f"At this step the full quadratic model is on the raw scale, with run {dev_run} at its recorded elution buffer pH (PD-005-03). "
                                     "The design was not augmented and has no block term. No effect, a selected model with the intercept only.")]
_re.show()
```

@tbl-adequacy judges each selected model against criteria 2, 3 and 4 of PCP-005 §7.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.CTable(header=[[T.C("Output", rs=2), T.C("Scale", rs=2), T.C("Terms", rs=2), T.C("R²", rs=2), T.C("Adj. R²", rs=2), T.C("Pred. R²", rs=2),
                  T.C("Criterion 2", cs=2), T.C("Criterion 3", cs=2), T.C("Criterion 4", cs=2)],
                 ["Model p", "Met", "LoF p", "Met", "Gap", "Met"]],
         body=adeq_body, align=["P{2.4cm}", "c", "P{1.6cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "c", "r", "c", "r", "c"],
         notes=[("", "Terms, the terms of the selected model besides the intercept. A, protein load. B, elution buffer pH. C, load flow rate. "
                     "D, end of pool collect. C², the square of C. AC, the interaction of A with C. "
                     "Criterion 2, the model F-test significant at α = " + g(eff_alpha) + " (n.a., a model with no term, which has no F-test). "
                     "Criterion 3, the lack of fit (LoF) test against pure error not significant at α = " + g(lof_alpha) + ". "
                     "Criterion 4, the gap, R² minus predicted R², at most " + f2(max_gap) + ".")],
         caption="Selected response-surface models against criteria 2, 3 and 4 of PCP-005 §7.", label="tbl-adequacy",
         size="footnotesize").show()
```

Each selected model meets criteria 3 and 4, and each model with a term meets criterion 2. The selection kept `{python} n_terms['pool_hcp_ng_mg']` of the `{python} n_terms_full` terms of the full quadratic model for pool host cell protein, `{python} n_terms['step_yield']` for step yield, `{python} n_terms['lmw_cesds_pct']` for fragments and none for leached Protein A.

### Pool host cell protein {#sec-rsm-hcp}

@tbl-coef-hcp gives the coefficients of the selected model for pool host cell protein, on the natural log scale, and @tbl-anova-hcp its analysis of variance.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(coef_df("pool_hcp_ng_mg"), "Response-surface coefficients for pool HCP, natural log of ng/mg, coded units.", "tbl-coef-hcp",
        align="lrrrr").show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(anova_df("pool_hcp_ng_mg"), "Analysis of variance with lack of fit for pool HCP, natural log of ng/mg.", "tbl-anova-hcp",
        align="lrrrrr").show()
```

Protein load and elution buffer pH carry the largest coefficients, `{python} f3(kA)` and `{python} mn(f3(kB))` per half range. Across the range studied pool host cell protein rises by a factor of `{python} f2(fac_A)` with protein load, and it falls by a factor of `{python} f2(fac_B)` as elution buffer pH rises from `{python} g(ph_lo)` to `{python} g(ph_hi)`. On the log scale the two effects add, so in ng/mg they multiply. With load flow rate and end of pool collect at their set-points, raising the pH across its range lowers pool host cell protein by `{python} f0(drop_hi_load)` ng/mg at a protein load of `{python} g(ld_hi)` g/L resin and by `{python} f0(drop_lo_load)` ng/mg at `{python} g(ld_lo)` g/L resin, at manufacturing scale. The factor is the same at both loads. In ng/mg the fall is larger at high load because the level it acts on is higher.

A model on the raw scale can describe two effects that multiply only through an interaction. In the full quadratic model on the raw scale the interaction of protein load with elution buffer pH is significant (`{python} pf(p_ab_raw)`), and the model of Version 1.0 carried it. In the full quadratic model on the log scale it is not significant (`{python} pf(p_ab_log)`), and the selected model does not contain it. The raw-scale interaction was therefore largely the multiplicative structure of the two main effects. Whether a further interaction of the two exists on the log scale the data do not decide. Its p-value is above `{python} g(eff_alpha)` in each of the three analyses of run `{python} dev_run`, and the selection keeps it in `{python} sens_ab_sel` of the `{python} len(SENS)` (@sec-dev01). @tbl-near-hcp lists the `{python} n_near` models whose AICc lies within 2 units of that of the selected model. All of them contain protein load, elution buffer pH and end of pool collect. They differ in load flow rate, in the interaction of protein load with elution buffer pH, and in the squares of the four factors. The interaction is in `{python} n_near_ab` of them, the nearest `{python} f2(near_d_ab)` units from the selected model, and its p-value is at least `{python} f3(near_pab_min)` in each. Models within 2 units of the lowest AICc have substantial support from the data [@burnham2002], so the data support each of these models about as well as the selected one.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_near_q = ["Yes" if (x["up"] <= C_HCP and x["up_lo"] <= C_HCP) else "No" for x in NEAR]
assert _near_q.count("No") == n_near_fail
_near_body = [r_ + [q_] for r_, q_ in zip(near_df.values.tolist(), _near_q)]
T.CTable(header=[[T.C("Terms", rs=2), T.C("ΔAICc", rs=2), T.C("Upper prediction limit over\nthe NOR, ng/mg", cs=2), T.C("Criteria\n2 to 4 met", rs=2),
                  T.C("Scale-down\nmodel\nqualified", rs=2)],
                 ["At the estimate", "At the low end"]],
         body=_near_body, align=["l", "r", "r", "r", "c", "c"],
         notes=[("", "Terms of the model besides the intercept, coded as in the factor legend. AB, the interaction of A with B. "
                     "A², B², C², D², the squares of A, B, C and D. ΔAICc, the AICc of the model minus that of the selected model, "
                     "the first row. AICc counts the residual variance as a parameter. At the estimate and at the low end, at "
                     "manufacturing scale over the NOR in force, with the offset ratio at its estimate and at the low end of its "
                     + off_ci + " % confidence interval. Scale-down model qualified, both limits within the criterion of ≤ "
                     + crit_hcp + " ng/mg.")],
         caption="Models of pool HCP within 2 AICc units of the selected model, log scale, with the upper prediction limit over the NOR.",
         label="tbl-near-hcp").show()
```

Each of these models meets criteria 2 to 4. With the offset ratio at its estimate, each gives an upper prediction limit over the NOR between `{python} f0(near_up_min)` and `{python} f0(near_up_max)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale, below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, so the conclusion over the NOR is the same whichever model is used. With the ratio at the low end of its interval each of the `{python} n_near` models exceeds the criterion, with limits between `{python} f0(near_lo_min)` and `{python} f0(near_lo_max)` ng/mg. With none of them is the scale-down model qualified for pool host cell protein over the NOR in force (@sec-sdm). That conclusion therefore does not depend on the choice of model.

End of pool collect lowers pool host cell protein. Its coefficient of `{python} mn(f3(kD))` per half range (`{python} pf(pD)`) is a fall of `{python} f"{fall_D:.0f}"` % across the range studied. Load flow rate has no significant linear effect (`{python} pf(pC)`). Its square is significant (`{python} pf(pC2)`), and pool host cell protein is higher at both ends of the flow range than at the set-point, by `{python} f"{flow_hi:.0f}"` % at `{python} g(P['flow'].prange[1])` cm/hr and `{python} f"{flow_lo:.0f}"` % at `{python} g(P['flow'].prange[0])` cm/hr. At the edges of the NOR of load flow rate the rise is at most `{python} f"{flow_nor:.0f}"` %. The lack of fit test (`{python} pf(fH['p_lof'])`) is not significant.

The effect of end of pool collect has opposite signs in the two designs. In the screening design it was `{python} f0(scr_D)` ng/mg across its range (`{python} pf(scr_D_p)`), and in the response-surface design it is a fall of `{python} f"{fall_D:.0f}"` %. The screening estimate is not significant, with a standard error of `{python} f0(scr_eff_se)` ng/mg. Noise alone does not explain the difference, however. The screening results were compared with the predictions of the response-surface model at the same settings. Their ratio rises with end of pool collect, by a factor of `{python} f2(disc_D_fac)` across its range (`{python} pf(disc_D_p)`). Curvature does not explain it either, because in a full factorial design the quadratic terms are confounded with the intercept, not with the main effect of end of pool collect. The cause was not identified (finding F11). A feed that carries more host cell protein in the tail of the elution peak would give the screening sign, because a later end of collection would then add host cell protein to the pool. The two designs were run at different times (@tbl-chronology), and their feeds were not characterized for this. The effect of end of pool collect is taken from the response-surface model, which is the predictive model.

Across the response-surface design pool host cell protein ranged from `{python} f0(hcp_all_min)` to `{python} f0(hcp_all_max)` ng/mg in the scale-down model. At manufacturing scale, `{python} n_hcp_over` results of the two designs exceeded the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, at `{python} f0(hcp_over_lo)` to `{python} f0(hcp_over_hi)` ng/mg. Each of them was at the highest protein load and the lowest elution buffer pH of the range studied, outside both NORs.

@fig-contours shows the response surfaces of the scale-down model over protein load and elution buffer pH, with load flow rate and end of pool collect at their set-points. In the pool host cell protein panel the contours are straight and parallel, because the selected model has no interaction of protein load with elution buffer pH. The contour levels are evenly spaced in ng/mg. Because the effects multiply, the bands between them are narrower where pool host cell protein is high, at high load and low pH. The leached Protein A panel is flat, because its selected model has no term.

```{python}
#| label: fig-contours
#| fig-cap: "Response surfaces of the scale-down model over protein load and elution buffer pH, with load flow rate and end of pool collect at their set-points (the design centre). Pool HCP, the median of the log-scale model. Step yield as a fraction. Leached Protein A, the mean of the runs, since its model has no term."
_fig = D.fig_rsm_contours(UO, xf="load", yf="elution_ph")
# the leached Protein A surface is a constant, and its colour bar carries one value
_cb = _fig.axes[-1]
_lo_, _hi_ = _cb.get_ylim()
_cb.set_yticks([(_lo_ + _hi_) / 2])
_cb.set_yticklabels([f"{lpa_mean:.2f}"])
_cb.yaxis.get_offset_text().set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

@fig-diag-hcp shows the diagnostics of the model on the log scale. The residuals scatter about zero across the predicted range without a funnel. On the normal probability plot they follow the line in the middle, and the largest positive residuals fall below it, so the upper tail of the residuals is shorter than that of a normal distribution. The lowest residual belongs to run `{python} dev_run`, at `{python} f1(dev_res_sd)` residual standard deviations below its prediction (@sec-dev01).

```{python}
#| label: fig-diag-hcp
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostics of the selected response-surface model for pool HCP, on the natural log scale."
_fig = D.fig_diagnostics(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
plt.show()
```

### Step yield {#sec-rsm-yield}

@tbl-coef-yield gives the coefficients of the selected model for step yield, in percentage points.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(coef_df("step_yield", k=100, nd=2), "Response-surface coefficients for step yield (percentage points), coded units.", "tbl-coef-yield",
        align="lrrrr").show()
```

End of pool collect has the largest effect. Extending it from `{python} g(P['end_collect'].prange[0])` to `{python} g(P['end_collect'].setpoint)` CV raises yield by `{python} f1(yD_lo_sp)` percentage points, and from `{python} g(P['end_collect'].setpoint)` to `{python} g(P['end_collect'].prange[1])` CV by a further `{python} f1(yD_sp_hi)` points. The negative square of end of pool collect makes the gain smaller at the upper end of its range. Protein load lowers yield by `{python} f2(abs(yA))` points per half range. At high load the coefficient of load flow rate is `{python} mn(f2(yC_hi))` points per half range, and at low load it is `{python} mn(f2(yC_lo))`. Flow rate therefore has almost no effect on yield when the bed has capacity to spare. Across the response-surface design step yield ranged from `{python} f1(y_min)` to `{python} f1(y_max)` %. @fig-diag-yield shows the diagnostics of the model.

In the designs and the univariate study, `{python} n_cap` results of step yield are exactly `{python} f1(100 * y_cap)` %, and none is higher. Of these, `{python} n_cap_ec` were at the upper end of the range of end of pool collect, `{python} g(P['end_collect'].prange[1])` CV. These results may reflect a limit on the reported yield. If they do, the gain at the upper end of end of pool collect is understated, and part of the negative square of end of pool collect may come from that limit.

### Leached Protein A {#sec-rsm-lpa}

The selected model of leached Protein A has no term. Within the range studied, leached Protein A does not depend on the `{python} n_fac` parameters of the multivariate design by more than the design resolves. With the `{python} n_rsm` runs and the scatter of this output, the half-width of the 95 % confidence interval of a main effect across the range studied is `{python} f2(lpa_mde)` ppm in a model of the four main effects. An effect smaller than this would not be told apart from zero. The model is the mean of the runs, `{python} f2(lpa_mean)` ppm in the scale-down model and `{python} f2(lpa_mean_m)` ppm at manufacturing scale. In the scale-down model leached Protein A ranged from `{python} f2(lpa_min)` to `{python} f2(lpa_max)` ppm across the runs of both designs. At manufacturing scale the highest result corresponds to `{python} f2(lpa_max_m)` ppm, and every run met the intermediate acceptance criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm (finding F5). These results use the re-assay of run `{python} dev_005_02_run`. With the first result of that run in its place, the selection keeps end of pool collect, and that model meets criteria 2 to 4 (@sec-dev02).

### Fragments by nrCE-SDS {#sec-rsm-frag}

@tbl-coef-frag gives the coefficients of the selected model for fragments by nrCE-SDS, measured on the `{python} fr_n` retained pools of the response-surface design.

```{python}

T.frame(coef_df("lmw_cesds_pct"), "Response-surface coefficients for fragments by nrCE-SDS (%), coded units.", "tbl-coef-frag",
        align="lrrrr").show()
```

The model is significant (`{python} pf(fF['p'])`), shows no significant lack of fit (`{python} pf(fF['p_lof'])`), and its predicted R² falls short of R² by `{python} f3(fF['gap'])`, within the limit of `{python} f2(max_gap)`. Its R² of `{python} f3(fF['R2'])` shows that most of the variation between pools is not explained by the parameters. Fragments fall as elution buffer pH rises, by `{python} f2(frag_eff_B)` percentage points across the range studied (`{python} pf(pFB)`). The selection also kept protein load, whose coefficient is not significant at α = `{python} g(eff_alpha)` (`{python} pf(pFA)`). AICc keeps a term when the improvement of the fit outweighs the penalty for its coefficient, and such a term need not be significant at α = `{python} g(eff_alpha)`. The effect of protein load on fragments is not interpreted. Over the NOR the upper prediction limit of a single run is `{python} f2(frag_nor_up)` %, against the intermediate acceptance criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_frag` %. Fragments ranged from `{python} f2(fr_min)` to `{python} f2(fr_max)` % across the pools, and every pool met the criterion. These results are in the scale-down model, because fragments carry no offset (@sec-sdm).

## Attributes measured for information

Aggregate by SEC was measured on every pool of both designs, for information. It ranged from `{python} f2(hmw_min)` to `{python} f2(hmw_max)` % HMW across the `{python} n_scr + n_rsm` pools, below the ≤ `{python} agg_crit` % that applies to the held eluate. Aggregate was not measured in the load, so these results do not show whether capture changes it. Appendix A and Appendix B give the individual results.

Residual DNA was measured on the load and the pool of the `{python} dna_n` centre-point runs of the two designs. With the antibody in the load measured by Protein A affinity HPLC, the load carried `{python} f0(dna_load_min)` to `{python} f0(dna_load_max)` pg per mg antibody, and the pool `{python} f0(dna_pool_min)` to `{python} f0(dna_pool_max)` pg/mg. That is a reduction of `{python} f1(dna_lrv_min)` to `{python} f1(dna_lrv_max)` log10 across the step. ## Model residuals and influential runs {#sec-resid}

@tbl-resid gives the residual checks of criterion 5 of PCP-005 §7 for the selected models.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(res_df, "Residual checks of the selected response-surface models (PCP-005 §7, criterion 5).", "tbl-resid",
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "c"],
        notes=[("", "Trend on predicted, the p-value of the regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values "
                    "(n.a., a model with no term predicts a single value). Trend on run order, the p-value of the regression "
                    "of the residuals on the run order of execution, which Appendix B gives. Cook's D, Cook's distance. Runs above " + cook_rule + ", "
                    "the number of runs with a Cook's distance above " + f2(cook_lim) + ", each examined by deleting it. F " + f_q_word + ", "
                    "the " + f_q_word + " of the F distribution with p and n − p degrees of freedom, p being the number of coefficients "
                    "of the model, above which a run fails it. Met, no trend significant at α = " + g(res_alpha) + " and no run above "
                    "the F " + f_q_word + ".")]).show()
```

Two of the `{python} n_trend_tests` trend tests are significant at α = `{python} g(res_alpha)`, so criterion 5 is not met for leached Protein A or for fragments on their trends. The residuals of leached Protein A rise with the run order of execution (`{python} pf(RES['leached_protein_a_ppm']['p_order'])`), by `{python} f2(lpa_drift)` ppm over the `{python} n_rsm` runs. That is `{python} f1(lpa_drift_pct)` % of the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm. The cause of the drift was not investigated. The absolute residuals of fragments rise with the predicted value (`{python} pf(RES['lmw_cesds_pct']['p_slope'])`), so the spread of the fragment results grows with their level. Across the range of the predictions the mean absolute residual grows by `{python} f2(frag_abs_change)` percentage points. The upper prediction limit of fragments over the NOR lies `{python} f2(frag_margin)` points below its criterion.

Every selected model has runs above the Cook's distance limit of `{python} cook_rule`, between `{python} n_over_min` and `{python} n_over_max` per output. The cut-off flags runs even when a model is correct. In data simulated from each selected model with normal residuals, it flags on average between `{python} f1(cook_sim_lo)` and `{python} f1(cook_sim_hi)` of the `{python} n_rsm` runs, and at least one run in `{python} f"{100 * cook_sim_p:.0f}"` to `{python} f"{100 * cook_sim_pmax:.0f}"` % of the data sets. A flagged run is therefore examined, and it fails the model only where its Cook's distance exceeds the `{python} f_q_word` of F(p, n − p), `{python} f2(f_lim_lo)` to `{python} f2(f_lim_hi)` for these models. No run exceeds it, and the largest Cook's distance is `{python} f2(cook_all_max)`. Criterion 5 is therefore met for pool host cell protein and step yield, and it is not met for leached Protein A and fragments, because of their residual trends.

For each output with a criterion, each run above `{python} cook_rule` was deleted in turn, the model selection repeated, and the output judged over the NOR again. For pool host cell protein these are runs `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in del_runs_hcp])`. With any one of them deleted, the upper prediction limit over the NOR lies between `{python} f0(del_hcp_lo)` and `{python} f0(del_hcp_hi)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale, against `{python} f0(pl_pt)` ng/mg with every run. Each of these is below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. With the offset at the low end of its interval the limit is `{python} f0(del_hcp_lo_end_min)` ng/mg with run `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in del_hcp_lo_run])` deleted, just within the criterion, and up to `{python} f0(del_hcp_lo_end)` ng/mg with either of the other runs deleted, as it is above the criterion with every run (@sec-sdm). Deleting a run is a test of its influence, and the qualification is judged on all runs. The coefficients of protein load and elution buffer pH change by at most `{python} f1(del_coef_pct)` %. Deleting run `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in del_changed])` adds the interaction of protein load with elution buffer pH and the square of protein load to the selected model (@sec-dev01). Run `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in del_changed])` therefore decides whether the selected model contains that interaction, but not the conclusion over the NOR. Leached Protein A with run `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in del_lpa_runs])` deleted, and fragments with run `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in del_frag_runs])` deleted, still meet their criteria at every combination of the NOR.

@tbl-uni gives the results of the univariate study S-PA-UNI for pool host cell protein, step yield and leached Protein A. Each end of each range is the arithmetic mean of `{python} uni_reps` runs. ## Hold study of the Protein A eluate {#sec-hold}

@tbl-hold-protein-a gives the results of the hold study.

```{python}

```

The study held one eluate, made at set-point with elution buffer pH `{python} g(hold_ph)`, and the two temperatures started from aliquots of it. On day 0 these aliquots already differed by `{python} f2(d0['hmw_pct'])` percentage points in aggregate, `{python} f1(d0['acidic_pct'])` points in acidic variants and `{python} f2(d0['lmw_cesds_pct'])` points in fragments by nrCE-SDS. This is the variation of the methods and of the aliquots, and a change smaller than it is not resolved.

Over `{python} h_days` days aggregate rose by `{python} f2(chg[(t_warm, 'hmw_pct')])` percentage points at `{python} t_warm` and `{python} f2(chg[(t_cold, 'hmw_pct')])` points at `{python} t_cold`. The faster rise when warm is consistent with partial unfolding at low pH. Fragments by nrCE-SDS rose by `{python} f2(chg[(t_warm, 'lmw_cesds_pct')])` points at `{python} t_warm`, more than the `{python} f2(d0['lmw_cesds_pct'])` points between the day 0 aliquots, which is consistent with faster hinge hydrolysis when warm. At `{python} t_cold` they changed by `{python} f3(frag_cold_raw)` points, `{python} frag_cold_word` the `{python} f3(frag_d0_raw)` points between the day 0 aliquots, which is not resolved. Acidic variants changed by `{python} f1(chg[(t_warm, 'acidic_pct')])` points at both temperatures, less than the `{python} f1(d0['acidic_pct'])` points between the day 0 aliquots. The hold therefore did not change acidic variants by more than the methods and aliquots resolve.

@tbl-hold-criterion judges the hold against the criteria of the low-pH inactivation load by the rule of @sec-holddesign, and acidic variants also against their lower limit.

        merge=["Attribute", "Limit", "Criterion", "Entering"], align=["P{2.6cm}", "l", "l", "r", "l", "r", "r", "c"],

For aggregate, acidic variants and fragments the largest increase at each temperature, added to the highest level expected in the pool, stays within the criterion of the low-pH inactivation load. On this evidence a hold of `{python} h_days` days at elution pH is supported at both `{python} t_cold` and `{python} t_warm` for an eluate made at set-point (finding F9). An eluate made at the low end of the elution buffer pH NOR, or one that carries more host cell protein, was not held. At a lower pH, aggregation and hinge hydrolysis are expected to be faster, and more host cell protein could bring more protease activity that clips the antibody. The results therefore do not show that the hold is supported for such an eluate.

The hold does not lower acidic variants. Their largest fall at any sample point was `{python} f1(abs(acid_fall))` points, no more than the `{python} f1(d0['acidic_pct'])` points between the two day 0 aliquots. The lower limit of `{python} g(acid_lim[0])` % is not met before the hold, at the least favourable corner of the production bioreactor NOR, with `{python} wc_acid_txt`. There the predicted median of acidic variants is `{python} f1(wc_acid['predicted'])` %, and the lower end of the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch is `{python} f1(exp_acid_lo)` %, below the limit. This is a result of the production bioreactor, not of the hold. The production bioreactor report PCR-003 accepts it as the producer's risk and reduces it with alarm limits on `{python} alarm_txt` inside the NOR on the side that lowers acidic variants, and with monitoring of acidic variants at harvest.

## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mech}

Pool host cell protein rises as elution buffer pH falls. A lower pH desorbs more of the host cell protein held weakly on the resin backbone and on the ligand, and this protein leaves the column with the product. On the log scale the pH effect is linear, so each step down in pH multiplies pool host cell protein by the same factor.

Pool host cell protein also rises with protein load, as in the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. PCP-005 assumed no mechanism for this rise (PCP-005 §4.1), and the designs do not test one. One explanation would give effects that multiply. Suppose a higher load leaves more host cell protein held weakly on the resin for each gram of antibody bound, and a lower elution pH releases a larger share of what is held. The host cell protein in the pool per mg of antibody is then the product of the two. The designs do not distinguish this explanation from others.

End of pool collect lowers pool host cell protein per mass of antibody. The weakly held impurity desorbs early, at the elution front, so collecting further into the tail of the peak adds antibody with little host cell protein. This does not explain why the effect had the opposite sign in the screening design (finding F11).

Pool host cell protein is slightly higher at both ends of the flow range than at the set-point. A short residence time at high flow lowers the dynamic binding capacity and broadens the mass transfer zone, which could raise pool host cell protein, but the same mechanism predicts no rise at low flow. The rise is at most `{python} f"{max(flow_lo, flow_hi):.0f}"` % across the range studied and `{python} f"{flow_nor:.0f}"` % within the NOR, and it is not interpreted further.

Step yield behaves as @sec-prior expected. Load flow rate costs yield only at high load, where the shorter residence time lets antibody break through near the capacity of the bed. The gain from extending the end of pool collect becomes smaller as the tail of the elution peak is exhausted, which is the negative square of the model.

Leached Protein A shows no dependence on the parameters within the range studied. Neither of the two opposite effects of protein load expected in @sec-prior, a longer exposure of the ligand to the harvest proteases and a dilution of the leached ligand over more antibody, is resolved against the variation of the runs. The offset of leached Protein A between the scales is expected to come from the protease activity of the held load, which is not a setting of a run (@sec-sdm).

Fragments by nrCE-SDS fall slightly as elution pH rises, which is the direction expected from acid-catalysed hinge hydrolysis during elution. The effect is small because the antibody spends only the duration of the elution at low pH in the column.

For operation, the risk to pool host cell protein lies at high protein load combined with low elution buffer pH, and never with every parameter of the multivariate design inside its NOR (@sec-ds). Within their NORs, end of pool collect moves pool host cell protein by `{python} f"{fall_D_nor:.0f}"` % and load flow rate by at most `{python} f"{flow_nor:.0f}"` %.

# Design space {#sec-ds}

The design space of this step is the region in protein load and elution buffer pH, the `{python} n_wc` WC-CPPs, over which a single batch is predicted to meet every intermediate acceptance criterion of the step. A point lies inside it when both ends of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run lie within the criterion of each quality attribute, at manufacturing scale where an offset applies. The criteria of this step are upper limits, so the upper prediction limit of @sec-stats decides, and at the boundary of the region a single batch is predicted to exceed the criterion with a probability of `{python} g(pi_tail)` %. Leached Protein A and fragments meet their criteria on this statistic everywhere in the range studied, and step yield has no criterion, so pool host cell protein alone bounds the region. The fractions below are of a grid of `{python} DS_N` points per factor over the range studied, with the offset of pool host cell protein at its estimate.

With load flow rate and end of pool collect at their set-points, the upper prediction limit meets the criterion over `{python} f1(ds2_sp)` % of the plane of protein load and elution buffer pH studied. It exceeds the criterion in the corner of high load and low pH, above a protein load of `{python} f1(ds_b_load)` g/L resin at pH `{python} g(ph_lo)` and below pH `{python} f2(ds_b_ph)` at `{python} g(ld_hi)` g/L resin. The excluded corner reaches into the protein load NOR and into the pH NOR, but never into both at once. It begins below pH `{python} f2(ds_b_ph_nor)` at the upper edge of the protein load NOR, `{python} g(P['load'].nor[1])` g/L resin, and above `{python} f1(ds_b_load_nor)` g/L resin at the lower edge of the pH NOR, `{python} g(P['elution_ph'].nor[0])`. The upper prediction limit is `{python} f0(corner_up)` ng/mg at the corner of high load and low pH of the range studied, and `{python} f0(nor_corner_up)` ng/mg at that corner of the two NORs. With load flow rate and end of pool collect at the corners of their NORs, between `{python} f1(ds2_nor_min)` and `{python} f1(ds2_nor_max)` % of the plane meets the criterion, and at the corners of their ranges studied between `{python} f1(ds2_rng_min)` and `{python} f1(ds2_rng_max)` %.

Over the whole range studied of all `{python} n_fac` factors, `{python} f1(ds_frac)` % of the grid lies inside the design space. The excluded points lie at a protein load of `{python} g(ds_load_min)` g/L resin or more with elution buffer pH `{python} f2(ds_ph_max)` or less. No point is excluded with every factor inside its NOR. With load flow rate and end of pool collect within their NORs, each excluded point lies outside the protein load NOR of `{python} nor(P['load'])` g/L resin or outside the pH NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])`. Inside both the protein load NOR and the pH NOR, a point is excluded only where load flow rate is outside its NOR. Most such points lie at a load flow rate of at most `{python} g(ds_ab_flow_max)` cm/hr with end of pool collect at most `{python} g(ds_ab_ec_max)` CV. The others lie at `{python} g(P['flow'].prange[1])` cm/hr, the upper end of the flow range studied, at a protein load of `{python} g(P['load'].nor[1])` g/L resin and end of pool collect at `{python} g(P['end_collect'].prange[0])` CV, the lower end of its range studied.

Drawn on the median prediction, for comparison only, the region would cover `{python} f1(dsm_frac)` % of the grid. A median can meet the criterion where a single batch does not.

Over the NOR the selected model predicts a median pool host cell protein of `{python} f0(hcp_nor_med_lo)` to `{python} f0(hcp_nor_med_hi)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale (@tbl-criteria-protein-a). The upper prediction limit reaches at most `{python} f0(pl_pt)` ng/mg over the NOR, below the criterion. Movement outside the NOR and within a PAR would be assessed under change control.

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

## Acceptance basis

Each output of the step is judged against the intermediate acceptance criterion that PCMP-001 §7.3 derives and that PCP-005 §8.1 applies to this step. The derivation is a priori, which here means that it uses the drug substance criteria and the platform worst cases of X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and no data from this campaign. The drug substance criterion is carried backward through the train with the worst case that each downstream step showed on the platform, and no margin is applied. PCMP-001 Version 2.0, which states this rule and the one below, took effect on `{python} pcmp_eff`, after every study of this report had ended.

PCMP-001 §7.5 then checks each platform worst case against the A-Mab results of its step. The check uses the one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single batch, at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the response-surface factors of the downstream step, on its unfavourable side. These are the NORs as characterized. The scale-down prediction of the downstream step is first taken to manufacturing scale with the offset of that step at its estimate, as PCMP-001 §7.1 rule 2 requires, so the check is made at manufacturing scale. Where the worst case that the model predicts within the NOR is worse than the platform value, the bound replaces the platform value and the criteria upstream become stricter. Where the bound is better than the platform value, and the model behind it meets the first three adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 (a significant model, no significant lack of fit and the limit on overfitting) and is not an exact fit, the bound replaces the platform value and the criteria upstream become wider. The fourth criterion, on the residuals and on influential runs, does not decide the change, and the report that gives the bound examines whether the bound depends on a single run. Otherwise the platform value stands. A point prediction never replaces it.

The bound is that of a single batch, not a confidence bound of the mean, for three reasons that PCMP-001 §7.5 gives. A quality attribute is judged on a single batch, and a single batch can fall beyond a bound of the mean. The platform worst case that the bound may replace was itself the result of a single run. A bound from a tolerance interval, which covers a stated share of all batches, would be statistically purer, but too conservative to set against a platform worst case of one run. @tbl-iac-verification gives the downstream values on which the criteria of this step rely.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.worst_case_verification(["viral_inactivation", "cex", "aex", "ufdf"]).show()
```

Each of the `{python} n_ver_rows` rows bears on this report. Host cell protein at cation exchange and anion exchange, fragments at low-pH viral inactivation and cation exchange, and leached Protein A at cation exchange and anion exchange set the criteria of the Protein A pool. Aggregate at low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange and UF/DF, and acidic variants at low-pH viral inactivation, set the criteria of the held eluate (@sec-holddesign). For acidic variants the single-batch bound of the low-pH increase is better than the platform value but does not replace it. The acidic variant results of the low-pH design have no scatter, so their model fits them exactly and cannot be judged adequate.

For pool host cell protein the drug substance limit of ≤ `{python} ds_hcp` ng/mg is carried back through cation exchange and anion exchange. With the platform worst cases of `{python} g(cex_req)`-fold and `{python} g(v_aex_hcp['assumed'])`-fold clearance, the a priori criterion was ≤ `{python} apri_hcp` ng/mg.

At cation exchange the platform worst case for host cell protein clearance stands. The cation exchange model, from the `{python} n_rsm_cex` runs of its response-surface design with `{python} cp_rsm_cex` centre points, predicts a lowest host cell protein clearance within its NOR of `{python} T.num(v_cex_hcp['predicted_nor'])`-fold, no worse than the platform value of `{python} g(cex_req)`-fold, so no criterion is tightened. Its single-batch bound, `{python} T.num(cex_bound)`-fold, is not better than the platform value, so none is widened.

At anion exchange the single-batch bound for host cell protein clearance replaced the platform worst case. The anion exchange model predicts a lowest clearance within its NOR of `{python} T.num(v_aex_hcp['predicted_nor'])`-fold, and its single-batch bound, `{python} T.num(aex_req)`-fold, is better than the platform value of `{python} g(v_aex_hcp['assumed'])`-fold. The model behind the bound meets the first three adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2. Its F-test is significant (`{python} pf(aex_fp)`), its lack of fit test is not (`{python} pf(aex_plof)`), and its predicted R² falls short of R² by `{python} f2(aex_gap)`, within the limit of `{python} f2(max_gap)`. The model is not an exact fit, and it meets the fourth criterion, because no run has a Cook's distance above the `{python} f_q_word` of F(p, n − p), `{python} f2(aex_flim)`. Runs `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in aex_cook_runs])` lie above `{python} cook_rule` and were examined. With each of runs `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in aex_cook_runs])` deleted in turn, and the model selection and the bound computed again, the selected model still met the three criteria and the bound stayed better than the platform value, at `{python} f2(aex_del_lo)` to `{python} f2(aex_del_hi)`-fold (`{python} INV2['id']` §8.4). The bound therefore does not depend on a single run. The bound comes from the `{python} n_rsm_aex` runs of the planned anion exchange design, with `{python} cp_rsm_aex` centre points. The criteria of this report were fixed when `{python} INV['id']` closed on `{python} INV['closed']`, before the `{python} n_aex_aug` runs that `{python} INV2['id']` added to that design were complete (study S-AEX-AUG, `{python} aex_aug_win`). On all `{python} n_aex_all` runs the bound is the same to three significant figures, `{python} T.num(va_aex['predicted_nor_bound95'])`-fold. For these reasons the clearance of anion exchange for A-Mab is known well enough to replace the platform value. The `{python} g(cex_req)`-fold of cation exchange and the `{python} T.num(aex_req)`-fold of anion exchange give a combined clearance of `{python} fold_hcp`-fold and the criterion in force of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, `{python} f"{widen_pct:.0f}"` % wider than the a priori value. At the edges of their ranges studied, outside their NORs, the lowest clearance measured in a run was `{python} f1(v_cex_hcp['observed_edge'])`-fold at cation exchange and `{python} f2(v_aex_hcp['observed_edge'])`-fold at anion exchange, both below their platform values. The criterion therefore relies on both steps running within their NORs (PCR-007, PCR-008).

The widening of the criterion for pool host cell protein is argued by its risk, in the four parts that PCMP-001 §7.5 asks for.

1. The risk is the producer's. A wider criterion admits a Protein A pool with more host cell protein, and a drug substance batch that then exceeded its criterion would be rejected at release.
2. An excursion would be detected at release of the drug substance, where host cell protein is tested by ELISA (AMV-3012). The limit of quantitation of the ELISA, `{python} g(hcp_loq)` ng/mg, is far below the criterion of ≤ `{python} ds_hcp` ng/mg. The coverage of the ELISA, the share of the host cell proteins that its antibodies recognise, is `{python} g(hcp_cov)` %, measured by `{python} hcp_cov_method` (AMV-3012). A host cell protein outside that share would not be detected by the release test.
3. A pool at the criterion meets the drug substance limit only if cation exchange clears at least `{python} g(cex_req)`-fold, to the cation exchange pool criterion of ≤ `{python} f0(crit_cex_hcp)` ng/mg, and anion exchange at least `{python} T.num(aex_req)`-fold. Cation exchange is credited with its platform value, which lies above its own single-batch bound of `{python} T.num(cex_bound)`-fold. If both steps cleared only their single-batch bounds, a pool at the criterion would give `{python} f0(ds_at_bounds)` ng/mg in the drug substance, above the limit. Over the NOR the upper prediction limit of a single pool is `{python} f0(pl_pt)` ng/mg, below the criterion.
4. In the integrated process model no simulated batch of `{python} f"{n_mc_b:,}"` exceeded the host cell protein criterion of the drug substance, and the normal tail probability is below one per million (@sec-cap).

The widening of the criterion for pool host cell protein rests on the model selection of `{python} INV2['id']` corrective action CA3. Without the model selection, the full quadratic model of anion exchange fails the limit on overfitting of PCMP-001 §7.2, with predicted R² `{python} f2(aex_full_gap)` below R², so no bound replaces a platform value, and the criterion would be the a priori value of ≤ `{python} f0(crit_wo)` ng/mg. Against that criterion, as against the criterion in force, the scale-down model would not be qualified for pool host cell protein (@sec-sdm). The NOR-propagated PAR of elution buffer pH for this output would be `{python} par_ph_wo` instead of `{python} par_ph_hcp`. No conclusion over the NOR would change.

For fragments the drug substance limit of ≤ `{python} ds_frag` % is carried back through cation exchange and then through the largest increase of low-pH viral inactivation, which gives ≤ `{python} crit_frag` %. Both point predictions confirm the platform values. Cation exchange is predicted to clear at least `{python} f2(v_cex_frag['predicted_nor'])`-fold within its NOR against `{python} fold_frag`-fold, and low-pH viral inactivation to add at most `{python} f3(v_vi_frag['predicted_nor'])` points against `{python} add_frag`. Neither single-batch bound is better than its platform value, at `{python} f2(v_cex_frag['predicted_nor_bound95'])`-fold and `{python} f3(v_vi_frag['predicted_nor_bound95'])` points, so both platform values stand and the criterion in force is the a priori value. Both fragment models also fail the limit of PCMP-001 §7.2 on how far predicted R² may fall below R², by `{python} f2(v_cex_frag['r2_minus_pred_r2'])` and `{python} f2(v_vi_frag['r2_minus_pred_r2'])` against `{python} f2(max_gap)`.

For leached Protein A the drug substance limit of ≤ `{python} ds_lpa` ppm is carried back through cation exchange and anion exchange, which together remove it `{python} fold_lpa`-fold on the platform. That gives ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm. Leached Protein A is not a response of the cation exchange or anion exchange designs. Its platform values therefore cannot be checked in this campaign, and they stand. No criterion upstream of this step uses a platform worst case of the Protein A step.

None of the `{python} n_crit` criteria of the Protein A pool was tightened. The aggregate criterion of the held eluate, the low-pH inactivation load, which the A-Mab results of cation exchange and low-pH viral inactivation changed, is derived in @sec-holddesign.

## Outputs against their criteria over the NOR

@tbl-criteria-protein-a gives each output at the set-point and over the NOR, as predicted by its selected model, and the 95 % limits of a single run over the NOR, which decide the verdict. Pool host cell protein and leached Protein A are at manufacturing scale. Fragments are in the scale-down model, because they carry no offset.

```{python}
#| output: asis
cr.notes = list(cr.notes) + [("", "Fragments carry no offset, and their values are those of the scale-down model.")]
cr.align = ["P{1.9cm}", "l", "r", "r", "r", "c"]      # the attribute names wrap, so the table and its notes keep the 8 pt floor
cr.show()
```

The `{python} n_crit` outputs with a criterion all meet it at the set-point and across the NOR in force. Each verdict rests on the upper end of those limits, the upper prediction limit of a single run over the NOR. It is `{python} f0(pl_pt)` ng/mg for pool host cell protein against ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, `{python} f2(lpa_nor_up)` ppm for leached Protein A against ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm, and `{python} f2(frag_nor_up)` % for fragments against ≤ `{python} crit_frag` %. The limit for pool host cell protein is taken with the offset ratio at its estimate. With the ratio at the low end of its interval it is `{python} f0(pl_lo)` ng/mg, above the criterion, and for this reason the scale-down model is not qualified for pool host cell protein over the NOR in force (@sec-sdm). The table gives medians for pool host cell protein, because its model is on the log scale. The model of leached Protein A has no term, so its prediction is the same at every setting.

## Proven acceptable ranges per attribute and parameter

@tbl-par gives the PAR of each parameter of the multivariate design for each output with a criterion, by the univariate analysis and by the NOR-propagated analysis of PCMP-001 §6.4. Every PAR spans the range studied of its parameter, except the NOR-propagated PAR of elution buffer pH for pool host cell protein. That PAR is `{python} par_ph_hcp`. Its lower end lies `{python} f3(par_ph_cut)` pH units inside the range studied, `{python} par_ph_steps_txt` of the grid of the analysis. The lower edge of the pH NOR lies `{python} f2(par_ph_margin)` pH units above the end of this PAR, and the set-point `{python} f2(par_ph_sp_margin)`.

```{python}

_hd1 = [T.C("Parameter", rs=2), T.C("Range\nstudied", rs=2)] + [T.C(f"{lab_} ≤ {c_} {u_}", cs=2) for _, lab_, c_, u_ in _out]

         label="tbl-par", size="footnotesize").show()
```

A PAR that reaches the edge of the range studied is reported as reaching it, and no claim is made beyond it (PCMP-001 §7.6). Each NOR-propagated PAR holds while the other parameters stay within their NORs. It does not cover two parameters at the edges of their ranges together. Towards the corner of high protein load and low elution buffer pH, beyond the NOR of at least one of the two, the upper prediction limit of pool host cell protein exceeds its criterion even with load flow rate and end of pool collect at their set-points (@sec-ds).
