# Process capability and robustness {#sec-cap}

@tbl-cap gives the capability at commercial scale, from the integrated process model of the train (@sec-stats), of the drug substance attributes to which this step contributes.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(cap_tab, "Commercial-scale capability of the drug substance attributes to which the Protein A step contributes.", "tbl-cap",
        align=["P{3.9cm}", "c", "l", "r", "l", "c", "r"],
        notes=[("a)", "Not meaningful, because the simulated values lie below the LOQ and cannot be measured."),
               ("b)", "Below the limit of quantitation (LOQ) of the ELISA, " + g(lpa_loq) + " ppm (AMV-3016)."),
               ("", "Crit., criticality. Mean and range of the " + mc_n + " simulated batches. Limiting side, the limit of the "
                    "criterion nearer to the simulated batches.")]).show()
```

Host cell protein and fragments have Cpk values of `{python} f2(cpk['hcp'])` and `{python} f2(cpk['fragments_lmw'])`, above the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` of PCMP-001 §7.9.

Residual DNA has no intermediate acceptance criterion. It is carried through the train in pg per mg of antibody and judged in the drug substance in ng per dose. The dose is the `{python} g(dose_mgkg)` mg/kg of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009] for an adult of `{python} g(dose_bw)` kg, `{python} f0(DOSE_MG)` mg of antibody. The body weight is an assumption of this report. In the simulation the drug substance carries at most `{python} _v(dna_ds_max)` ng per dose against the criterion of ≤ `{python} g(dna_crit)` ng per dose, a Cpk of `{python} f2(cpk['residual_dna'])`. The integrated process model carries a nominal DNA reduction for each chromatography step, `{python} g(dna_lrv_cfg['protein_a'])` log10 at Protein A, `{python} g(dna_lrv_cfg['cex'])` at cation exchange and `{python} g(dna_lrv_cfg['aex'])` at anion exchange. The platform history gives no worst-case DNA clearance for these steps (@sec-prior), so the Cpk of residual DNA rests on these nominal values. At this step the reduction measured at the centre points, `{python} f1(dna_lrv_min)` to `{python} f1(dna_lrv_max)` log10, is at or below the nominal value. At anion exchange every pool of the response-surface design was below the limit of quantitation of the qPCR, `{python} g(dna_loq)` pg/mg (AMV-3014), so the reduction there is not measured. Each run shows only that it exceeds the DNA in its load over that limit, between `{python} f1(aex_dna_lb_min)` and `{python} f1(aex_dna_lb_max)` log10 (PCR-008). The Cpk of residual DNA therefore rests on a nominal anion exchange reduction that the data of this campaign do not measure.

No simulated batch of `{python} mc_n` fell outside the drug substance criterion for host cell protein, leached Protein A, fragments or residual DNA. With none of `{python} mc_n` outside, the probability of an out-of-specification batch in the simulation is below `{python} f2(oos_bound)` % at `{python} f"{100 * conf:.0f}"` % confidence. The bound does not include the uncertainty of the integrated process model itself.

The Cpk of leached Protein A is not meaningful. The simulated drug substance values average `{python} g(lpa_ds_mean)` ppm, below the limit of quantitation of the ELISA (`{python} g(lpa_loq)` ppm, AMV-3016). They cannot be measured, and their spread is that of the model, not of a result. Leached Protein A is judged instead against its criteria in the pool (@sec-par) and in the drug substance.

Acidic variants have the lowest Cpk of the drug substance, `{python} f2(cpk['acidic_variants'])`, set by the lower limit of `{python} g(acid_lim[0])` %. This is below the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` and above the minimum of `{python} f2(CPK_MIN)` of PCMP-001 §7.9, which asks PCMR-001 to state the parameters that drive it. In the simulation `{python} acid_oos` batch of `{python} mc_n` fell outside the criterion, and the normal tail probability is `{python} f0(acid_ppm)` per million. The Protein A step does not separate charge variants. The hold of the eluate does not lower acidic variants (@sec-hold), so it does not move them towards the lower limit that sets the Cpk.

# Parameter classification {#sec-class}

Parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7, as PCP-005 §7 applies it (criterion 7). An attribute is affected by a parameter when a term of the selected model that contains the parameter is significant at α = `{python} g(eff_alpha)` (PCMP-001 §6.2). A parameter whose effect on a CQA is significant and practically relevant is critical. A critical parameter is a WC-CPP when it has a low risk of leaving its acceptable range in operation, because it is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR, and a CPP otherwise. A KPP affects process performance and has no relevant effect on a CQA, and a GPP has no relevant effect on either. A significant effect that is too small to move the attribute appreciably within the PAR does not by itself make a parameter critical. Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a numerical threshold for a practically relevant effect or for a low risk. Each class below is therefore argued from the size of each effect across the PAR, stated beside its significance, and from the margin of the PAR to the NOR. The effect on pool host cell protein is given at manufacturing scale with the other parameters at their set-points, and as a share of its criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg.

- Protein load was classified as a WC-CPP. Its terms are significant for pool host cell protein, `{python} termp('load', 'pool_hcp_ng_mg')`, and for step yield, `{python} termp('load', 'step_yield')`, but not for fragments (`{python} pf(_tp['lmw_cesds_pct']['A'])`). Across its PAR for pool host cell protein, which is its range studied of `{python} rng(P['load'])` g/L resin, pool host cell protein rises from `{python} f0(CLE['load']['v_lo'])` to `{python} f0(CLE['load']['v_hi'])` ng/mg, a change of `{python} f"{CLE['load']['pct']:.0f}"` % of the criterion. Together with elution buffer pH it takes pool host cell protein above its criterion within the range studied, and `{python} n_hcp_over` results of the designs at the corner of high load and low pH exceeded the criterion (@sec-rsm-hcp). The effect is therefore practically relevant, and protein load is critical. The load is set from the load volume and the titre of the clarified harvest by Protein A affinity HPLC (AMV-3021), so it is readily controlled, and its PAR extends `{python} g(CLE['load']['m_lo'])` g/L resin below and `{python} g(CLE['load']['m_hi'])` g/L resin above its NOR of `{python} nor(P['load'])` g/L resin. Over that NOR the scale-down model is not qualified for pool host cell protein, and the NOR is flagged for discussion with manufacturing (@sec-sdm).
- Elution buffer pH was classified as a WC-CPP. Its terms are significant for pool host cell protein, `{python} termp('elution_ph', 'pool_hcp_ng_mg')`, and for fragments, `{python} termp('elution_ph', 'lmw_cesds_pct')`, and step yield has no term in it. Across its PAR for pool host cell protein, `{python} par_ph_hcp`, pool host cell protein falls from `{python} f0(CLE['elution_ph']['v_lo'])` to `{python} f0(CLE['elution_ph']['v_hi'])` ng/mg as the pH rises, a change of `{python} f"{CLE['elution_ph']['pct']:.0f}"` % of the criterion. Fragments fall by `{python} f2(frag_eff_B)` percentage points across their PAR, the range studied, `{python} f"{frag_pct:.0f}"` % of their criterion. The effect on pool host cell protein is practically relevant, and with protein load it bounds the design space. Buffer pH is controlled at preparation and verified at release, and the PAR for pool host cell protein extends `{python} f2(CLE['elution_ph']['m_lo'])` pH units below and `{python} f2(CLE['elution_ph']['m_hi'])` above the NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])`. The study event DEV-005-01 showed that a buffer below the NOR can pass release when the pH meter is incorrectly calibrated (@sec-dev01). The buffer of that event, at pH `{python} g(dev_005_01_ph_measured)`, lay below the NOR and inside the PAR.
- Load flow rate was classified as a KPP. Its terms are significant for step yield, `{python} termp('flow', 'step_yield')`, and for pool host cell protein, `{python} termp('flow', 'pool_hcp_ng_mg')`. It costs step yield at high load, up to `{python} f1(y_flow_hi)` percentage points across its range studied at `{python} g(P['load'].prange[1])` g/L resin, because a faster load shortens the residence time and lowers the dynamic binding capacity. Its effect on pool host cell protein is the curvature, a change of at most `{python} f0(CLE['flow']['span'])` ng/mg across its PAR, the range studied of `{python} rng(P['flow'])` cm/hr, or `{python} f"{CLE['flow']['pct']:.0f}"` % of the criterion, and of at most `{python} f"{flow_nor:.0f}"` % within the NOR. That effect is significant but too small to move pool host cell protein appreciably within the PAR, so it does not make load flow rate critical. The PAR extends `{python} g(CLE['flow']['m_lo'])` cm/hr below and `{python} g(CLE['flow']['m_hi'])` cm/hr above the NOR of `{python} nor(P['flow'])` cm/hr. No effect of load flow rate on leached Protein A or fragments was detected within the range studied.
- End of pool collect was classified as a KPP. Its terms are significant for step yield, `{python} termp('end_collect', 'step_yield')`, and for pool host cell protein, `{python} termp('end_collect', 'pool_hcp_ng_mg')`. It has the largest effect on step yield, a gain of `{python} f1(y_span['end_collect'])` percentage points across its range studied. Across its PAR for pool host cell protein, the range studied of `{python} rng(P['end_collect'])` CV, it lowers pool host cell protein from `{python} f0(CLE['end_collect']['v_lo'])` to `{python} f0(CLE['end_collect']['v_hi'])` ng/mg, a change of `{python} f"{CLE['end_collect']['pct']:.0f}"` % of the criterion, and the sign of that effect differs between the designs (finding F11). That effect is significant but too small to move pool host cell protein appreciably within the PAR, so it does not make end of pool collect critical. The PAR extends `{python} g(CLE['end_collect']['m_lo'])` CV below and `{python} g(CLE['end_collect']['m_hi'])` CV above the NOR of `{python} nor(P['end_collect'])` CV. The class would be revisited if a later study confirmed the screening sign.
- Operating temperature was classified as a GPP. No difference from the set-point runs was detected in pool host cell protein, step yield or leached Protein A at either end of its range. The intervals allow a rise in pool host cell protein of up to `{python} f0(uni_ub['temperature'])` ng/mg. Such a rise would still leave pool host cell protein within its criterion at manufacturing scale, and every individual result met its criterion (@sec-uni). The range studied of `{python} rng(P['temperature'])` °C, which these results support, extends `{python} g(uni_m['temperature'][0])` °C below and `{python} g(uni_m['temperature'][1])` °C above the NOR of `{python} nor(P['temperature'])` °C. The class rests on the attributes measured. Fragments were not measured by nrCE-SDS in the univariate study (@sec-uni), so for fragments the class rests on the mechanism and on the response-surface model. A higher temperature is expected to speed acid-catalysed hinge hydrolysis during elution. In the response-surface design fragments changed by `{python} f2(frag_eff_B)` percentage points across the whole range of elution buffer pH, the condition that drives that hydrolysis (@sec-rsm-frag). Their upper prediction limit over the NOR lies `{python} f2(frag_margin)` points below the criterion. The class assumes that a change of temperature within its range studied does not use up that margin, and this was not tested.
- Bed height was classified as a GPP. No difference from the set-point runs was detected in pool host cell protein, step yield or leached Protein A at either end of its range. The intervals allow a rise in pool host cell protein of up to `{python} f0(uni_ub['bed_height'])` ng/mg, and every individual result met its criterion (@sec-uni). The range studied of `{python} rng(P['bed_height'])` cm, which these results support, extends `{python} g(uni_m['bed_height'][0])` cm below and `{python} g(uni_m['bed_height'][1])` cm above the NOR of `{python} nor(P['bed_height'])` cm. Bed height is fixed by the packing specification of the commercial column and does not vary in operation. A short bed at the upper end of the load range was not characterized, and no claim is made for it. The class rests on the attributes measured. Fragments were not measured by nrCE-SDS in the univariate study (@sec-uni), so for fragments the class rests on the mechanism and on the response-surface model. A fragment that carries Fc binds the ligand as the intact antibody does, so a shorter residence time is expected to lower the capture of both alike. In the response-surface design no effect of load flow rate on fragments was detected over residence times from `{python} g(rt_hi)` to `{python} g(rt_lo)` min, at the set-point bed height (@sec-rsm-frag). The shortest bed gives `{python} g(rt_short)` min, below that span, and no fragment result supports the class there.

In summary the step has `{python} n_wc` WC-CPPs, `{python} n_kpp` KPPs and `{python} n_gpp` GPPs. `{python} "No parameter is in the class CPP" if n_cpp == 0 else f"{n_cpp} parameters are in the class CPP"`. The two WC-CPPs are critical parameters that are well controlled. The classes of protein load and elution buffer pH rest on the size of their effects on pool host cell protein within the PAR and on the corner where the two together take it above its criterion. Both effects agree in direction with the A-Mab case study. Load flow rate and end of pool collect also have significant effects on pool host cell protein, each too small to make the parameter critical. The KPP classes rest on the model for step yield, on the direction of the yield effects in both designs, and on the mechanism of breakthrough and of peak collection.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-cs}

The Protein A step contributes to the control strategy in the following ways.

1. Process parameters. Protein load and elution buffer pH are controlled within their NORs as WC-CPPs, and load flow rate and end of pool collect within their NORs as KPPs. The NORs are those of PCP-005. Over the NOR of protein load the scale-down model is not qualified for pool host cell protein, and that NOR is flagged for discussion with manufacturing on whether it can be improved (@sec-sdm). Movement outside the NOR and within the PARs of @sec-par is assessed under change control.
2. Material controls. Elution buffer is released against its pH specification, on a calibrated pH meter (DEV-005-01).
3. Resin and load. The protein load is set from the titre of the clarified harvest by Protein A affinity HPLC (AMV-3021). Leached Protein A is highest on new resin and is expected to rise with the protease activity of the load. Resin use, cleaning and sanitization are controlled by SOP-2008. The hold of the clarified harvest before capture, the expected cause of the offset of leached Protein A between the scales, is characterized in PCR-004.
4. Hold. An eluate made at set-point may be held at elution pH for up to `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm` before viral inactivation. An eluate made at other settings within the NOR was not held (@sec-hold).
5. Downstream clearance. Host cell protein, leached Protein A and fragments are further cleared by cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008). The criterion for pool host cell protein relies on cation exchange clearing host cell protein at least `{python} g(cex_req)`-fold, its platform worst case, and anion exchange at least `{python} T.num(aex_req)`-fold, its single-batch bound, while both run within their NORs (@sec-par). Host cell protein is tested at release of the drug substance. Viral clearance is claimed at low-pH viral inactivation (PCR-006), anion exchange and virus filtration (PCR-009), and not at this step.

The control strategy of the whole train is consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The characterization confirms the main effects expected for this step. Elution buffer pH and protein load have the largest effects on pool host cell protein, and on the log scale their effects multiply. Whether a further interaction of the two exists the data do not decide (@sec-rsm-hcp). End of pool collect, protein load and load flow rate have the largest effects on step yield. Leached Protein A shows no dependence on the parameters within the range studied, and fragments depend only slightly on elution buffer pH. End of pool collect lowers pool host cell protein in the response-surface design but raised it, not significantly, in the screening design, for a reason that was not identified.

Model selection gave leached Protein A and fragments models that meet the adequacy criteria on lack of fit and predictive power, which their full quadratic models do not. The choice of model is a discrepancy from the plan, so its effect on the conclusions was examined. The conclusion over the NOR is the same with each of the `{python} n_near` models within 2 AICc units of the selected model of pool host cell protein, and with run `{python} dev_run` analysed in each of three ways.

Over the NOR in force the scale-down model is not qualified for pool host cell protein. The conclusion holds with the offset ratio at its estimate and fails at the low end of its interval, at the upper end of the protein load NOR. This does not depend on the criterion, on the `{python} n_sd_supp` set-point runs added after the planned runs had been analysed, or on the choice of model (@sec-sdm). The NOR is not narrowed, because NORs come from production. It is flagged for discussion with manufacturing on whether it can be improved, and the limit at the low end of the ratio meets the criterion when the upper edge of the protein load NOR is `{python} f1(load_q_max)` g/L resin. The offsets were estimated at set-point only. The report therefore assumes that the ratio for pool host cell protein and the difference for leached Protein A are the same across the ranges studied, and this assumption is not tested. Fragments have no measured offset. Their conclusions assume no difference between the scales, on the mechanism of capture and on the bound from the hold study of the clarified harvest (@sec-sdm).

The criterion for pool host cell protein links this step to the two later steps. It credits cation exchange with its platform worst case of `{python} g(cex_req)`-fold, above the single-batch bound of `{python} T.num(cex_bound)`-fold of its A-Mab model, and anion exchange with its single-batch bound of `{python} T.num(aex_req)`-fold. The control of this step therefore depends on the control of those steps (PCR-007, PCR-008), and an excursion would be detected at release of the drug substance (@sec-par).

The models of leached Protein A and fragments fail criterion 5 on a residual trend, and their conclusions rest on its size (PD-005-02). The re-assay of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` decides whether leached Protein A depends on end of pool collect, but not its judgement against the criterion (@sec-dev02). Each design used one feed, so the effect of feed quality was not estimated. The univariate study cannot detect interactions, has `{python} uni_reps` runs at each end and no centre run (PD-005-07), and did not measure fragments by nrCE-SDS. The hold study held one eluate, made at set-point.

# Conclusions

1. The step was characterized under PCP-005 in a screening design, a response-surface design and a univariate study.
2. The scale-down model is qualified by its offset for leached Protein A. Over the NOR in force, with protein load at `{python} nor(P['load'])` g/L resin, it is not qualified for pool host cell protein. The conclusion holds with the offset ratio at its estimate and fails at the low end of its interval. The NOR is not narrowed. It is flagged for discussion with manufacturing on whether it can be improved.
3. Each selected model of the response-surface outputs meets the adequacy criteria on lack of fit and predictive power, and each model with a term is significant. Criterion 5 is met except for leached Protein A and fragments, whose residual trends are small against their criteria (PD-005-02).
4. Elution buffer pH and protein load have the largest effects on pool host cell protein, and their main effects multiply. Leached Protein A shows no dependence on the parameters within the range studied, on the re-assay of run `{python} dev_005_02_run`, and fragments fall slightly as elution buffer pH rises.
5. The criterion for pool host cell protein, ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, is widened by the single-batch bound of anion exchange. The widening is the producer's risk, and an excursion would be detected at release of the drug substance.
6. Each output with a criterion met it across the NOR in force, pool host cell protein with the offset ratio at its estimate. Every NOR-propagated PAR spans the range studied of its parameter, except that of elution buffer pH for pool host cell protein, `{python} par_ph_hcp`. The design space, drawn on the upper prediction limit of a single run, covers `{python} f1(ds_frac)` % of the range studied and excludes no point with every parameter inside its NOR.
7. Protein load and elution buffer pH are WC-CPPs, load flow rate and end of pool collect are KPPs, and operating temperature and bed height are GPPs. No parameter is in the class CPP.
8. The ranges studied of operating temperature and bed height are supported for pool host cell protein, step yield and leached Protein A, with the other parameters at their set-points.
9. In a hold study of the Version 2.0 re-analysis, what a `{python} h_days`-day hold at elution pH at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm` added to an eluate made at set-point kept aggregate, acidic variants and fragments `{python} hold_rule_word` the upper limits of the low-pH inactivation load. The hold did not lower acidic variants, which can enter it below their lower limit (PCR-003).
10. At commercial scale the Cpk of host cell protein and of fragments exceeds the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)`.
11. Neither study event changes the judgement of an output against its criterion. The results roll up into PCMR-001.

Each was investigated, and its run was retained in the analysis.

## DEV-005-01. Elution buffer pH below target on a response-surface run {#sec-dev01}

The elution buffer of lot `{python} dev_lot` was used on run `{python} dev_run` of the response-surface design, whose design setting for elution buffer pH was `{python} g(dev_ph_design)`. During preparation the titration of the buffer overshot its end point, and the buffer was at pH `{python} g(dev_005_01_ph_measured)`, `{python} f2(dev_ph_gap)` pH units below its target. It passed release because the pH meter used for release was incorrectly calibrated and read it within its specification. The recorded pH is below the NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])` and inside the range studied of `{python} rng(P['elution_ph'])`.

Run `{python} dev_run` is analysed at its recorded pH, the setting at which it was made. PCP-005 planned every run at its design setting, so this is the discrepancy from the plan PD-005-03 (@sec-dev). The run gave a pool host cell protein of `{python} f0(dev_obs_m)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale, below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. On the selected model its residual is `{python} mn(f2(dev_res))` on the natural log scale. The result is therefore `{python} f"{dev_res_pct:.0f}"` % below the median predicted at pH `{python} g(dev_ph_rec)`, `{python} f0(dev_pred_rec)` ng/mg, which is `{python} f1(dev_res_sd)` residual standard deviations. Its Cook's distance, `{python} f2(dev_cook)`, is above the limit of `{python} cook_rule`. At the design pH of `{python} g(dev_ph_design)` the same model predicts `{python} f0(dev_pred_des)` ng/mg, closer to the result. The result does not show the full rise in pool host cell protein that a buffer at the recorded pH would be expected to cause. The data do not establish why.

@tbl-dev01 gives the conclusion for pool host cell protein with run `{python} dev_run` analysed in three ways, each with the model selection repeated.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(sens_df, "Selected model of pool HCP and its upper prediction limit over the NOR (ng/mg, manufacturing scale) with run " + str(dev_run) + " analysed in three ways.", "tbl-dev01",
        align=["P{4.4cm}", "c", "P{3.9cm}", "r", "r", "c"],
        notes=[("", "Terms of the selected model besides the intercept, coded as in the factor legend. AB, the interaction of A with B. "
                    "A², C², the squares of A and C. At the estimate and at the low end, the upper prediction limit with the offset "
                    "ratio at its estimate and at the low end of its interval. Scale-down model qualified, both limits within the criterion of ≤ "
                    + crit_hcp + " ng/mg.")]).show()
```

With run `{python} dev_run` at its design pH, or excluded, the log scale is chosen again, and the selection adds the interaction of protein load with elution buffer pH and the square of protein load. The interaction is not significant in the full quadratic model on the log scale in any of the three analyses (`{python} pf(SENS['recorded']['p_ab'])`, `{python} f3(SENS['design']['p_ab'])` and `{python} f3(SENS['excluded']['p_ab'])`). Nor is it significant in the two selected models that contain it (`{python} pf(SSEL['design']['p_ab'])` and `{python} f3(SSEL['excluded']['p_ab'])`). In the selected model with the run at its design pH the square of protein load is negative (`{python} pf(sens_a2['p_a2'])`), so in that analysis the rise of pool host cell protein with load levels off at high load. In all three analyses pool host cell protein meets its criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg at every combination of the NOR with the offset ratio at its estimate, and exceeds it with the ratio at the unfavourable end of its interval. The scale-down model is therefore not qualified for pool host cell protein however run `{python} dev_run` is analysed. The analysis at the recorded pH gives the highest upper prediction limit of the three. The run was retained, and it carries a footnote in Appendix B.

## DEV-005-02. Leached Protein A result of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` initially out of trend {#sec-dev02}

The leached Protein A result of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` of the response-surface design was out of trend at analytical review. By the rule in the record of the event, a result is out of trend when it lies outside the two-sided `{python} oot_pct` % prediction interval of a single result from the full quadratic model of the response-surface design, fitted to the other runs of the design without the result under review, at the settings of the run. The review was made when the design ran, before model selection was adopted on `{python} ca3_date`, so it used the model that PCP-005 specifies. For run `{python} dev_005_02_run` the interval, from the other `{python} n_oot` runs with `{python} oot_df` residual degrees of freedom, runs from `{python} mn(f2(oot_lo))` to `{python} f2(oot_hi)` ppm in the scale-down model. Its lower end lies below zero, so at this run only a high result could be out of trend. The first result, `{python} f2(dev02_first)` ppm (`{python} f2(dev02_first_m)` ppm at manufacturing scale), lay above the interval and above every other result of the two designs. The sample was re-assayed under AMV-3016. The re-assay, `{python} f2(dev02_val)` ppm (`{python} f2(dev02_m)` ppm at manufacturing scale), lay inside the interval and inside the range of the other runs of the response-surface design, `{python} f2(others_min)` to `{python} f2(others_max)` ppm. The first result was `{python} g(first_ratio)` times the re-assay. The investigation suspected carryover in the ELISA, which would add analyte from a preceding sample, and did not confirm it. The re-assay result is the one reported in Appendix B and used in the analysis, because the investigation attributed the first result to that suspected cause. The first result was kept in the record with its status marked. Both results are far below the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm.

With the first result in place of the re-assay, the analysis changes. The model selection then puts leached Protein A on the log scale and keeps end of pool collect, and that model meets criteria 2 to 4. Its F-test is significant (`{python} s02_ptxt`), its lack of fit test is not (`{python} pf(s02_plof)`), and its predicted R² falls short of R² by `{python} f3(s02_gap)`. On that model leached Protein A would fall by `{python} f"{s02_fall:.0f}"` % across the range of end of pool collect. Its upper prediction limit over the NOR would be `{python} f2(s02_nor_up)` ppm at manufacturing scale, against `{python} f2(lpa_nor_up)` ppm with the re-assay, and every PAR would still span the range studied of its parameter. The trend of the residuals on run order would not be significant (`{python} pf(order_p_first)`). The judgement of leached Protein A against its criterion is therefore the same with either result. The class of end of pool collect would not change, because that effect, `{python} f2(s02_chg)` ppm across its range against the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm, is too small to move leached Protein A appreciably (@sec-class). Whether leached Protein A depends on end of pool collect, and whether its residuals drift with run order, depends on which result is used.

## Discrepancies from the plan

The report records `{python} n_pd` discrepancies from the plan, which @tbl-pd, @tbl-pd-b and @tbl-pd-c list with what PCP-005 planned, what was done and why. They are judged against PCP-005 Version 2.0, the plan this report is written against. That version includes the retest of retained samples, S-PA-RET, made under the method decision AMD-001, so S-PA-RET is not a discrepancy. Four discrepancies change how the runs are analysed or measured and are described where their results are reported. They are the use for the ranges and the design space of the models of leached Protein A and fragments, which do not meet criterion 5 (PD-005-02, @sec-resid), run `{python} dev_run` analysed at its recorded elution buffer pH (PD-005-03, @sec-dev01), the model selection in place of the full quadratic model of PCP-005 §5.5 (PD-005-04, @sec-stats), and the loaded antibody mass of step yield taken from the titre by Protein A affinity HPLC in place of absorbance at 280 nm, because absorbance measures every protein in a clarified harvest and not the antibody alone (PD-005-06, @sec-methods). Two are further studies, and three are departures from the plan found in the Version 2.0 review of the record. The sixth is the use of the model of pool host cell protein against a rule of PCMP-001 §7.1. These six are described below.

### PD-005-01. Supplementary set-point runs in the scale-down model qualification {#sec-pd01}

PCP-005 planned `{python} n_sd_plan` set-point runs of the scale-down model in the qualification study S-PA-SDM, compared with `{python} n_m` manufacturing-scale batches. During the Version 2.0 re-analysis, while INV-001 was open, a further `{python} n_sd_supp` set-point runs were made in study S-PA-SDM2 (`{python} win('S-PA-SDM2')`). @tbl-sdm-offsets-planned gives the qualification on the `{python} n_sd_plan` planned runs alone.

On the planned runs alone the scale-down model is not qualified for pool host cell protein over the NOR in force. The ratio is `{python} rt0_hcp` (`{python} rt0_hcp_lo` to `{python} rt0_hcp_hi`) on the planned runs and `{python} rt_hcp` (`{python} rt_hcp_lo` to `{python} rt_hcp_hi`) on all runs. With the ratio at the low end of the wider interval, the upper prediction limit over the NOR is `{python} f0(pl_lo0)` ng/mg, above the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, while at the estimate of the ratio the criterion is met. The further runs narrowed the half-width of the interval on the log scale by `{python} f"{narrow_pct:.0f}"` %. On all runs the limit with the ratio at its low end is `{python} f0(pl_lo)` ng/mg, still above the criterion, so the model is not qualified for pool host cell protein on all runs either (@sec-sdm). For leached Protein A the model is qualified on the planned runs as well, with the scale-down model `{python} lpa0_off` ppm lower (`{python} lpa0_off_a` to `{python} lpa0_off_b` ppm lower).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets(["protein_a"], studies=["S-PA-SDM"], label="tbl-sdm-offsets-planned").show()
```

The decision to make the runs was taken during the re-analysis, after the result on the planned runs was known. Runs added after a result was seen raise the chance that a test passes. Here the model is not qualified for pool host cell protein on all runs either, so the added runs did not change the outcome of the qualification. The rule of qualification and the criterion were not changed because of the further runs. Only the number of runs grew. The centre points of the designs are also set-point runs of the scale-down model. They were not added to the offset, because PCP-005 §5.1 defines the qualification on the runs of the qualification study.

### PD-005-05. Hold study of the Protein A eluate {#sec-pd05}

PCP-005 planned no hold study, and Version 1.0 reported no hold result. During the Version 2.0 re-analysis, after INV-001 closed, the eluate was held in study S-PA-HLD (`{python} win('S-PA-HLD')`), because Version 2.0 judges a held intermediate against its intermediate acceptance criteria. The plan set no hold criterion, because it foresaw no hold study, so the rule that judges the held eluate against the criteria of the low-pH inactivation load is part of this discrepancy. The study and the rule are described in @sec-holddesign and the results in @sec-hold. They support a hold of `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm` for an eluate made at set-point.

### PD-005-07. Univariate study without runs at the centre {#sec-pd07}

PCP-005 §6.4 requires each parameter of the univariate study to be run at the low edge, the centre and the high edge of its range studied, with the same responses as in the multivariate designs. Study S-PA-UNI (`{python} win('S-PA-UNI')`) ran each end of each range `{python} uni_reps` times and made no run at the centre. The `{python} uni_n_ref` set-point runs of the qualification study S-PA-SDM (`{python} win('S-PA-SDM')`) served as the reference instead. The departure was found in the Version 2.0 review of the study record against PCP-005, and the runs were retained. Without the centre runs the study has no set-point reference of its own. A difference from the reference therefore combines the effect of the parameter with any difference between the two studies. Step yield was higher than the reference at every end of both ranges (@sec-uni), which is consistent with such a difference. The judgement of pool host cell protein and leached Protein A rests on the individual results at both ends, each against its criterion, and does not depend on the reference.

### PD-005-08. Leached Protein A offset of the scale-down model accounted for, not investigated {#sec-pd08}

PCP-005 Version 1.0 accepted the scale-down model for an output only where the qualification showed no difference between the scales significant at α = `{python} g(eff_alpha)`, and it required any difference to be investigated and the model modified before the characterization studies. On the `{python} n_sd_plan` scale-down runs of study S-PA-SDM against the `{python} n_m` manufacturing-scale batches, leached Protein A differs between the scales under that test (`{python} pf(dev04_p)`, two-sided Student t test with pooled variance). No other output that the qualification compared differs at that level. The difference was not investigated before the characterization studies. The departure was found in the Version 2.0 re-analysis of the qualification against the Version 1.0 rule. PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.1 lets a scale-down model differ in mean from manufacturing scale where its offset is known precisely enough, so the Version 1.0 test was stricter than the use of the model needs. Leached Protein A is judged through its offset, and the model is qualified for it on the planned runs and on all runs (@sec-sdm, @sec-pd01). The expected cause of the difference, the longer hold of the load at manufacturing scale, is stated in @sec-sdm and was not tested.

### PD-005-09. Univariate study made before the response-surface design {#sec-pd09}

PCP-005 §11 sets the order of the work. The qualification runs come first, the screening design second and the response-surface design third, and the univariate assessments come fourth and may run in parallel with the response-surface design. Study S-PA-UNI ran from `{python} chron.loc['S-PA-UNI', 'start']` to `{python} chron.loc['S-PA-UNI', 'end']`, after the screening design ended on `{python} chron.loc['S-PA-SCR', 'end']` and before the response-surface design began on `{python} chron.loc['S-PA-RSM', 'start']` (@tbl-chronology). The departure was found in the Version 2.0 review of the execution dates (INV-001 finding 5), and the runs were retained. The reason recorded is the `{python} pd09_reason`. The univariate study is judged on its own runs and on the set-point runs of the qualification study, and no result of the response-surface design depends on it, so the order changes no conclusion of this report.

### PD-005-10. Pool host cell protein model used although its conclusion changes across the offset interval {#sec-pd10}

PCMP-001 §7.1 states that a model whose conclusion for an output changes between the two ends of the offset interval is not used for that output. Over the NOR in force the upper prediction limit of a single run of pool host cell protein is `{python} f0(pl_pt)` ng/mg with the offset ratio at its estimate and `{python} f0(pl_lo)` ng/mg with the ratio at the low end of its interval, against the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg (@sec-sdm). The conclusion therefore changes across the interval. The model is used all the same for the judgement over the NOR, for the PARs and for the design space, with the ratio at its estimate as PCMP-001 §7.1 rule 2 requires. The offset is known precisely enough to be accounted for at its estimate. The NOR comes from production and is not narrowed by an offset. The limitation is stated with each conclusion for pool host cell protein, and the protein load NOR is flagged for discussion with manufacturing, so that manufacturing can decide whether the NOR can be improved.

```{python}
#| output: asis
# the register, set in three parts so that each fits a page at the 8 pt floor; the rows are the builder's, unchanged
_pdr = md_rows(discrepancy_register(DOC))
assert list(_pdr.iloc[:, 0]) == list(PDS)
_pd_cut, _pd_cut2 = list(PDS).index("PD-005-05"), list(PDS).index("PD-005-08")
pd_a = _pdr.iloc[:_pd_cut].reset_index(drop=True)
pd_b = _pdr.iloc[_pd_cut:_pd_cut2].reset_index(drop=True)
pd_c = _pdr.iloc[_pd_cut2:].reset_index(drop=True)
T.frame(pd_a, f"Discrepancies of this report from its plan PCP-005, {pd_a.iloc[0, 0]} to {pd_a.iloc[-1, 0]}.", "tbl-pd",
        align=["l", "P{2.2cm}", "P{3.0cm}", "P{4.6cm}", "P{3.3cm}"], size="footnotesize").show()
```

        align=["l", "P{2.2cm}", "P{3.0cm}", "P{4.6cm}", "P{3.3cm}"], size="footnotesize").show()
